The classification — removable, pole of order m, or essential singularity — is determined by how many negative-power terms are present. The residue Res[f, z₀] is the coefficient of (z−z₀)^{−1}. The residue theorem states that the integral of f around any closed contour equals 2πi times the sum of residues at the enclosed singularities. hook: |
  The integral $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{\cos x}{1+x^2}\,dx$ resists
  every standard technique — substitution and integration by parts lead
  nowhere. Treated as a contour integral in the complex plane, it reduces
  to a residue calculation that takes three lines. The answer is $\pi/e$.

  The residue theorem converts an integral over the real line — or over
  any closed curve in the plane — into a sum of local contributions from
  singularities. Each singularity contributes exactly $2\pi i$ times its
  residue. Finding residues is algebra, not integration.

  The tool that makes this possible is the Laurent series: the power
  series that works near a singularity by including negative powers of
  $(z-z_0)$. The residue is the coefficient of $(z-z_0)^{-1}$.

## Taylor series for analytic functions

If $f$ is analytic in a disk $|z - z_0| < R$, it has a **Taylor series** that converges in that disk:

$$f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n(z-z_0)^n, \qquad c_n = \frac{f^{(n)}(z_0)}{n!} = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_C \frac{f(z)}{(z-z_0)^{n+1}}\,dz$$

The series converges absolutely for $|z - z_0| < R$ and uniformly on any closed subdisk. The radius of convergence $R$ equals the distance from $z_0$ to the nearest singularity of $f$.

**Key Taylor series** (centred at 0, valid for all $z$):

$$e^z = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{n!}, \qquad \sin z = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n z^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}, \qquad \cos z = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n z^{2n}}{(2n)!}$$

$$\frac{1}{1-z} = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} z^n \quad (|z| < 1)$$

These are exactly the real Taylor series with $x$ replaced by $z$.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // Taylor series convergence disk — missed opportunity 1
  // Draggable z₀, disk of radius R = distance to nearest singularity
  const W = 480, H = 420, CX = 200, CY = 210, SCALE = 70;
  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  const funcSel = Inputs.select([
    "1/(z²+1)  — poles at ±i",
    "tan z      — poles at ±π/2, ±3π/2, …",
    "log z      — branch cut on Re≤0",
    "e^z        — entire (no singularity)"
  ], { value: "1/(z²+1)  — poles at ±i", label: "f(z)" });

  const nTermsSl = Inputs.range([1, 20], { value: 6, step: 1, label: "Partial sum N" });

  // z₀ position via sliders (dragging complex in OJS needs canvas events; sliders are cleaner)
  const z0reSl = Inputs.range([-2.5, 2.5], { value: 0.5, step: 0.05, label: "Re(z₀)" });
  const z0imSl = Inputs.range([-2.5, 2.5], { value: 0.3, step: 0.05, label: "Im(z₀)" });

  function singularities(fname) {
    if (fname.startsWith("1/(z²+1)")) return [{re:0,im:1},{re:0,im:-1}];
    if (fname.startsWith("tan")) {
      const s = [];
      for (let k = -3; k <= 3; k++) s.push({re: (k+0.5)*Math.PI, im: 0});
      return s;
    }
    if (fname.startsWith("log")) return [{re:-99,im:0}]; // branch cut; treat as nearest on negative axis
    return []; // entire
  }

  function nearestDist(fname, z0re, z0im) {
    if (fname.startsWith("log")) {
      // Distance to nearest branch-cut point on {Re≤0} = distance to point (-|z0re|, z0im) if z0re<0 else to (0, z0im)
      // Approximate: distance to origin along the branch cut direction
      // The branch cut is the negative real axis; nearest point is (min(z0re,0), 0) extended
      // Actually: the branch point is at z=0, and the branch cut extends left.
      // Convergence radius of Taylor series at z0 = distance to origin (the branch point)
      return Math.sqrt(z0re*z0re + z0im*z0im);
    }
    const sings = singularities(fname);
    if (sings.length === 0) return 999; // entire
    let minD = Infinity;
    for (const s of sings) {
      const d = Math.sqrt((z0re-s.re)**2 + (z0im-s.im)**2);
      if (d < minD) minD = d;
    }
    return minD;
  }

  function evalFunc(fname, re, im) {
    if (fname.startsWith("1/(z²+1)")) {
      const a = 1 + re*re - im*im, b = 2*re*im;
      const d = a*a + b*b; if (d < 1e-10) return [NaN, NaN];
      return [a/d, -b/d];
    }
    if (fname.startsWith("tan")) {
      const sr = Math.sin(re)*Math.cosh(im), si = Math.cos(re)*Math.sinh(im);
      const cr = Math.cos(re)*Math.cosh(im), ci = -Math.sin(re)*Math.sinh(im);
      const d = cr*cr + ci*ci; if (d < 1e-10) return [NaN, NaN];
      return [(sr*cr+si*ci)/d, (si*cr-sr*ci)/d];
    }
    if (fname.startsWith("log")) {
      const r2 = re*re + im*im; if (r2 < 1e-10) return [NaN, NaN];
      return [0.5*Math.log(r2), Math.atan2(im, re)];
    }
    // e^z
    return [Math.exp(re)*Math.cos(im), Math.exp(re)*Math.sin(im)];
  }

  function taylorCoeffs(fname, z0re, z0im, N) {
    // Numerical Taylor coefficients via finite differences (central diff for accuracy)
    // c_n = f^(n)(z0) / n!  — computed by repeated complex differentiation
    // We use forward differences with h = 0.001 * R direction
    const h = 0.001;
    const coeffs = []; // [re, im] for n=0..N-1
    // Use complex differentiation formula: f'(z) ≈ (f(z+h) - f(z-h)) / (2h)
    // We'll just evaluate directly for known functions
    if (fname.startsWith("1/(z²+1)")) {
      // f(z) = 1/(z²+1); f^(n)(z0) computable
      // Use the partial fraction decomposition: f = i/2 * (1/(z+i) - 1/(z-i))
      // 1/(z-a)^{n+1} contributes (-1)^n * n! / (z0-a)^{n+1} to n-th derivative
      const c = []; // coefficients c_n for Taylor at z0
      const amre = z0re, amim = z0im + 1; // z0 - (-i) = z0 + i
      const apre = z0re, apim = z0im - 1; // z0 - i
      const amd = amre*amre + amim*amim;
      const apd = apre*apre + apim*apim;
      if (amd < 1e-10 || apd < 1e-10) return null;
      // c_n = i/2 * [(-1)^n n! / (z0-(-i))^{n+1} - (-1)^n n! / (z0-i)^{n+1}]
      // = i/2 * (-1)^n n! * [1/(z0+i)^{n+1} - 1/(z0-i)^{n+1}]
      // Power of complex: (a+ib)^k
      function cpow(re, im, k) {
        if (k === 0) return [1, 0];
        let r = Math.sqrt(re*re+im*im), theta = Math.atan2(im, re);
        let rk = Math.pow(r, k), tk = theta * k;
        return [rk*Math.cos(tk), rk*Math.sin(tk)];
      }
      function cdiv(ar, ai, br, bi) {
        const d = br*br + bi*bi; if (d < 1e-12) return [NaN, NaN];
        return [(ar*br+ai*bi)/d, (ai*br-ar*bi)/d];
      }
      for (let n = 0; n < N; n++) {
        const [pm_re, pm_im] = cpow(amre, amim, n+1);
        const [pp_re, pp_im] = cpow(apre, apim, n+1);
        const [inv_am_re, inv_am_im] = cdiv(1, 0, pm_re, pm_im);
        const [inv_ap_re, inv_ap_im] = cdiv(1, 0, pp_re, pp_im);
        // diff = inv_am - inv_ap
        const diffRe = inv_am_re - inv_ap_re, diffIm = inv_am_im - inv_ap_im;
        // multiply by i/2 and (-1)^n (n! already absorbed into c_n = f^(n)(z0)/n!)
        // c_n = i/2 * (-1)^n * [diff]   (the n! cancels with 1/n!)
        const sign = (n%2===0) ? 1 : -1;
        // * i/2: (a+ib)*i = -b+ia
        const cr = sign * (-diffIm) / 2;
        const ci = sign * (diffRe) / 2;
        c.push([cr, ci]);
      }
      return c;
    }
    // Fallback: numerical coefficients via repeated evaluation
    // f^(n)(z0) ≈ (2h)^{-n} * sum_k C(n,k)*(-1)^{n-k} f(z0 + k*h) — forward differences
    // For simplicity, use a simple numerical approach
    const c = [];
    for (let n = 0; n < N; n++) {
      // n-th derivative via central finite differences (Richardson extrapolation would be better but expensive)
      const hn = Math.pow(0.01, 1); // step
      let sumRe = 0, sumIm = 0;
      // Forward difference: f^(n)(z0) ≈ (1/h^n) sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^{n-k} C(n,k) f(z0 + k*h)
      let fact = 1;
      for (let k = 0; k <= n; k++) {
        const sign = ((n-k)%2===0) ? 1 : -1;
        const binom = fact / ((k <= n-k ? [1,1,2,6,24,120,720,5040][k]||1 : [1,1,2,6,24,120,720,5040][n-k]||1) * ([1,1,2,6,24,120,720,5040][Math.min(k,n-k)]||1));
        const [fr, fi] = evalFunc(fname, z0re + k*hn, z0im);
        // C(n,k) = n! / (k! * (n-k)!)
        let cn = 1; for (let j=0;j<n;j++) cn*=(j<k?1:1); // just accumulate properly
        // Simple binomial
        let bk = 1; for (let j=0;j<k;j++) bk = bk*(n-j)/(j+1);
        sumRe += sign * bk * fr;
        sumIm += sign * bk * fi;
      }
      let nfact = 1; for (let j=1;j<=n;j++) nfact*=j;
      c.push([sumRe / Math.pow(hn, n) / nfact, sumIm / Math.pow(hn, n) / nfact]);
    }
    return c;
  }

  function taylorPartialSum(coeffs, z0re, z0im, re, im, N) {
    // Sum c_n (z - z0)^n
    const dre = re - z0re, dim = im - z0im;
    let sumRe = 0, sumIm = 0;
    let powRe = 1, powIm = 0;
    for (let n = 0; n < Math.min(coeffs.length, N); n++) {
      const [cr, ci] = coeffs[n];
      sumRe += cr*powRe - ci*powIm;
      sumIm += cr*powIm + ci*powRe;
      const newPowRe = powRe*dre - powIm*dim;
      const newPowIm = powRe*dim + powIm*dre;
      powRe = newPowRe; powIm = newPowIm;
    }
    return [sumRe, sumIm];
  }

  function hslToRgb(h, s, l) {
    h = ((h%1)+1)%1;
    const c = (1-Math.abs(2*l-1))*s, x = c*(1-Math.abs((h*6)%2-1)), m = l-c/2;
    let r=0,g=0,b=0;
    if(h<1/6){r=c;g=x;}else if(h<2/6){r=x;g=c;}else if(h<3/6){g=c;b=x;}
    else if(h<4/6){g=x;b=c;}else if(h<5/6){r=x;b=c;}else{r=c;b=x;}
    return [Math.round((r+m)*255),Math.round((g+m)*255),Math.round((b+m)*255)];
  }

  function toScreen(re, im) { return [CX + re*SCALE, CY - im*SCALE]; }

  function render(fname, z0re, z0im, N) {
    const R = nearestDist(fname, z0re, z0im);
    const coeffs = taylorCoeffs(fname, z0re, z0im, N) || [];

    // Left panel: exact function with disk overlay
    const cL = document.createElement("canvas");
    cL.width = W; cL.height = H;
    const ctxL = cL.getContext("2d");
    const imgL = ctxL.createImageData(W, H); const dL = imgL.data;

    for (let px=0; px<W; px++) {
      for (let py=0; py<H; py++) {
        const re = (px-CX)/SCALE, im = -(py-CY)/SCALE;
        const [wr, wi] = evalFunc(fname, re, im);
        if (!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)||isNaN(wr)) {
          const idx=(py*W+px)*4;
          dL[idx]=255;dL[idx+1]=255;dL[idx+2]=255;dL[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const arg = Math.atan2(wi, wr), mag = Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue = (arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const brightness = 0.5 + 0.35*Math.tanh(Math.log(mag+0.001)/2);
        const [r,g,b] = hslToRgb(hue, 0.8, brightness);
        const idx=(py*W+px)*4; dL[idx]=r;dL[idx+1]=g;dL[idx+2]=b;dL[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    ctxL.putImageData(imgL, 0, 0);

    // Convergence disk — gold dashed circle
    const [z0sx, z0sy] = toScreen(z0re, z0im);
    ctxL.setLineDash([6, 4]);
    ctxL.strokeStyle = "#fbbf24"; ctxL.lineWidth = 2.5;
    ctxL.beginPath();
    if (R < 50) ctxL.arc(z0sx, z0sy, R*SCALE, 0, 2*Math.PI);
    ctxL.stroke();
    ctxL.setLineDash([]);

    // Line to nearest singularity
    const sings = singularities(fname);
    if (sings.length > 0) {
      let nearS = sings[0], nearD = Infinity;
      for (const s of sings) {
        const d = Math.sqrt((z0re-s.re)**2+(z0im-s.im)**2);
        if (d < nearD) { nearD = d; nearS = s; }
      }
      const [nsx, nsy] = toScreen(nearS.re, nearS.im);
      ctxL.strokeStyle = "rgba(251,191,36,0.6)"; ctxL.lineWidth = 1.5; ctxL.setLineDash([3,3]);
      ctxL.beginPath(); ctxL.moveTo(z0sx, z0sy); ctxL.lineTo(nsx, nsy); ctxL.stroke();
      ctxL.setLineDash([]);
      // Nearest singularity ×
      ctxL.strokeStyle="#ef4444"; ctxL.lineWidth=2;
      ctxL.beginPath(); ctxL.moveTo(nsx-6,nsy-6); ctxL.lineTo(nsx+6,nsy+6); ctxL.stroke();
      ctxL.beginPath(); ctxL.moveTo(nsx+6,nsy-6); ctxL.lineTo(nsx-6,nsy+6); ctxL.stroke();
    }

    // Axes
    const [ox, oy] = toScreen(0, 0);
    ctxL.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.5)"; ctxL.lineWidth=0.8;
    ctxL.beginPath(); ctxL.moveTo(0,oy); ctxL.lineTo(W,oy); ctxL.stroke();
    ctxL.beginPath(); ctxL.moveTo(ox,0); ctxL.lineTo(ox,H); ctxL.stroke();

    // z₀ dot
    ctxL.fillStyle="#fbbf24"; ctxL.beginPath(); ctxL.arc(z0sx, z0sy, 6, 0, 2*Math.PI); ctxL.fill();
    ctxL.strokeStyle="#fff"; ctxL.lineWidth=1.5; ctxL.stroke();
    ctxL.fillStyle="#fff"; ctxL.font="11px sans-serif";
    ctxL.fillText(`z₀`, z0sx+8, z0sy-4);
    ctxL.fillText(`R = ${R < 50 ? R.toFixed(3) : "∞"}`, z0sx+8, z0sy+10);

    ctxL.fillStyle="rgba(0,0,0,0.7)"; ctxL.font="11px sans-serif";
    ctxL.fillText("exact f(z)", 6, 16);

    // Right panel: partial sum
    const cR = document.createElement("canvas");
    cR.width = W; cR.height = H;
    const ctxR = cR.getContext("2d");
    const imgR = ctxR.createImageData(W, H); const dR = imgR.data;

    for (let px=0; px<W; px++) {
      for (let py=0; py<H; py++) {
        const re = (px-CX)/SCALE, im = -(py-CY)/SCALE;
        let wr, wi;
        if (coeffs.length > 0) {
          [wr, wi] = taylorPartialSum(coeffs, z0re, z0im, re, im, N);
        } else {
          [wr, wi] = evalFunc(fname, re, im);
        }
        if (!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)||isNaN(wr)||Math.abs(wr)>200||Math.abs(wi)>200) {
          const idx=(py*W+px)*4;
          dR[idx]=240;dR[idx+1]=240;dR[idx+2]=240;dR[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const arg = Math.atan2(wi, wr), mag = Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue = (arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const brightness = 0.5 + 0.35*Math.tanh(Math.log(mag+0.001)/2);
        const [r,g,b] = hslToRgb(hue, 0.8, brightness);
        const idx=(py*W+px)*4; dR[idx]=r;dR[idx+1]=g;dR[idx+2]=b;dR[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    ctxR.putImageData(imgR, 0, 0);

    // Disk overlay on right panel
    ctxR.setLineDash([6,4]);
    ctxR.strokeStyle="#fbbf24"; ctxR.lineWidth=2.5;
    ctxR.beginPath();
    if (R < 50) ctxR.arc(z0sx, z0sy, R*SCALE, 0, 2*Math.PI);
    ctxR.stroke(); ctxR.setLineDash([]);
    ctxR.fillStyle="#fbbf24"; ctxR.beginPath(); ctxR.arc(z0sx, z0sy, 6, 0, 2*Math.PI); ctxR.fill();
    ctxR.strokeStyle="#fff"; ctxR.lineWidth=1.5; ctxR.stroke();
    const [ox2, oy2] = toScreen(0, 0);
    ctxR.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.5)"; ctxR.lineWidth=0.8;
    ctxR.beginPath(); ctxR.moveTo(0,oy2); ctxR.lineTo(W,oy2); ctxR.stroke();
    ctxR.beginPath(); ctxR.moveTo(ox2,0); ctxR.lineTo(ox2,H); ctxR.stroke();
    ctxR.fillStyle="rgba(0,0,0,0.7)"; ctxR.font="11px sans-serif";
    ctxR.fillText(`Taylor partial sum, N=${N} terms`, 6, 16);
    ctxR.fillStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.85)"; ctxR.font="10px sans-serif";
    ctxR.fillText("Inside disk: series matches f. Outside: diverges.", 6, H-8);

    const panelDiv = document.createElement("div");
    panelDiv.style.cssText = "display:flex; gap:0.75rem; flex-wrap:wrap;";
    panelDiv.appendChild(cL); panelDiv.appendChild(cR);

    const infoDiv = document.createElement("div");
    infoDiv.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.88em; background:#fefce8; border:1px solid #fde68a; border-radius:4px; padding:0.5rem 0.75rem;";
    infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong>Convergence radius R = ${R < 50 ? R.toFixed(4) : "∞"}</strong> — distance from z₀ = ${z0re.toFixed(2)}+${z0im.toFixed(2)}i to nearest singularity. The Taylor series converges inside the gold dashed disk and diverges outside it.`;

    const wrap = document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(panelDiv); wrap.appendChild(infoDiv);
    return wrap;
  }

  const container = document.createElement("div");
  container.style.cssText = "border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const title = document.createElement("div");
  title.style.cssText = "font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  title.textContent = "Taylor series convergence disk: R = distance to nearest singularity";
  container.appendChild(title);
  container.appendChild(funcSel);
  container.appendChild(z0reSl);
  container.appendChild(z0imSl);
  container.appendChild(nTermsSl);
  const vizDiv = document.createElement("div");
  container.appendChild(vizDiv);
  const note = document.createElement("div");
  note.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  note.textContent = "Left: exact f(z) with domain colouring (hue = arg f, brightness = log|f|). Right: N-term Taylor partial sum at z₀. Gold dashed circle = convergence disk of radius R. Red × = nearest singularity. Move z₀ or change N to watch the disk and partial sum update.";
  container.appendChild(note);

  function update() {
    vizDiv.innerHTML = "";
    vizDiv.appendChild(render(funcSel.value, z0reSl.value, z0imSl.value, nTermsSl.value));
  }
  funcSel.addEventListener("input", update);
  z0reSl.addEventListener("input", update);
  z0imSl.addEventListener("input", update);
  nTermsSl.addEventListener("input", update);
  update();

  return container;
}
```

## Laurent series

At a point $z_0$ where $f$ is not analytic, the Taylor series does not converge. The **Laurent series** extends the power series to include negative powers:

$$f(z) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} c_n(z-z_0)^n$$

where the coefficients are:

$$c_n = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_C \frac{f(z)}{(z-z_0)^{n+1}}\,dz$$

This converges in an **annulus** $r < |z - z_0| < R$ (with $r$ possibly 0 and $R$ possibly $\infty$).

The **principal part** consists of the negative-power terms $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} c_{-n}(z-z_0)^{-n}$; the **analytic part** is the non-negative power series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}c_n(z-z_0)^n$. Whether the principal part is absent, has finitely many terms, or has infinitely many terms classifies the type of singularity at $z_0$ — which is the point of the next section.

<!-- STUDENT: The terms "principal part" and "analytic part" are introduced here but their significance is not explained until the classification section two paragraphs later. A reader might wonder why the split matters. A forward pointer — "the number of terms in the principal part will classify the singularity" — would make this naming feel purposeful immediately. -->

<!-- VIZ OPPORTUNITY 9: Laurent series convergence in an annulus. Rewritten per senior-designer brief. -->

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const W = 400, H = 360, CX = W/2, CY = H/2, SCALE = 66;
  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  const funcSel9 = Inputs.select(["1/(z(z-1))", "e^{1/z} (essential)", "z/sin(z)"], {
    value: "1/(z(z-1))", label: "f(z)"
  });
  const rInnerSl = Inputs.range([0.01, 1.4], {value: 0.2, step: 0.01, label: "Inner barrier r"});
  const rOuterSl = Inputs.range([0.5, 3.5], {value: 1.5, step: 0.05, label: "Outer barrier R"});
  const nTermsSl = Inputs.range([1, 20], {value: 6, step: 1, label: "N terms (e^{1/z} panel)"});

  // Singularity metadata per function
  const funcMeta = {
    "1/(z(z-1))": {
      sings: [{re:0,im:0,label:"z=0 (simple pole)"},{re:1,im:0,label:"z=1 (simple pole)"}],
      ppTerms: 2, singType: "Two simple poles", annulusDesc: "0 < |z| < 1 (between poles)"
    },
    "e^{1/z} (essential)": {
      sings: [{re:0,im:0,label:"z=0 (essential)"}],
      ppTerms: Infinity, singType: "Essential singularity (infinitely many principal-part terms)", annulusDesc: "0 < |z| < ∞"
    },
    "z/sin(z)": {
      sings: [{re:0,im:0,label:"z=0 (removable)"},{re:Math.PI,im:0,label:"z=π (simple pole)"},{re:-Math.PI,im:0,label:"z=−π (simple pole)"}],
      ppTerms: 1, singType: "Removable at 0; simple poles at ±nπ", annulusDesc: "0 < |z| < π"
    }
  };

  function evalExact9(fname, re, im) {
    switch(fname) {
      case "1/(z(z-1))": {
        const d2=re*re+im*im; if(d2<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
        const dr=re-1,di=im,d3=dr*dr+di*di; if(d3<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
        return [dr/d3-re/d2, -di/d3+im/d2];
      }
      case "e^{1/z} (essential)": {
        const d=re*re+im*im; if(d<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
        const invRe=re/d, invIm=-im/d;
        return [Math.exp(invRe)*Math.cos(invIm), Math.exp(invRe)*Math.sin(invIm)];
      }
      case "z/sin(z)": {
        const sr=Math.sin(re)*Math.cosh(im), si=Math.cos(re)*Math.sinh(im);
        const d=sr*sr+si*si; if(d<1e-8) return (re*re+im*im<1e-8)?[1,0]:[NaN,NaN];
        return [(re*sr+im*si)/d, (im*sr-re*si)/d];
      }
      default: return [NaN,NaN];
    }
  }

  function evalPartial9(fname, re, im, N) {
    // Genuine N-term partial sums of Laurent series at z0=0
    switch(fname) {
      case "1/(z(z-1))": {
        // For 0<|z|<1: -1/z - 1 - z - z^2 - ... (principal part: -1/z; analytic: -sum z^n)
        const d=re*re+im*im; if(d<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
        const invRe=re/d, invIm=-im/d;
        // -1/z term
        let sumRe = -invRe, sumIm = -invIm;
        // -z^n terms for n=0..N-2
        let powRe=1, powIm=0;
        for(let k=0;k<N-1;k++) {
          sumRe -= powRe; sumIm -= powIm;
          const nRe=powRe*re-powIm*im; const nIm=powRe*im+powIm*re;
          powRe=nRe; powIm=nIm;
        }
        return [sumRe, sumIm];
      }
      case "e^{1/z} (essential)": {
        const d=re*re+im*im; if(d<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
        const invRe=re/d, invIm=-im/d;
        let sumRe=1, sumIm=0, powRe=1, powIm=0, fact=1;
        for(let k=1;k<=Math.min(N,25);k++) {
          const nRe=powRe*invRe-powIm*invIm; const nIm=powRe*invIm+powIm*invRe;
          powRe=nRe; powIm=nIm; fact*=k;
          sumRe+=powRe/fact; sumIm+=powIm/fact;
        }
        return [sumRe, sumIm];
      }
      case "z/sin(z)": {
        // Laurent around 0: z/sin(z) = 1 + z²/6 + 7z⁴/360 + ...  (all non-negative powers; removable sing)
        // Treat as Taylor (no principal part)
        const coeffs=[1, 0, 1/6, 0, 7/360, 0, 31/15120, 0, 127/604800, 0];
        let sumRe=0, sumIm=0, powRe=1, powIm=0;
        for(let k=0;k<Math.min(N,coeffs.length);k++) {
          sumRe+=coeffs[k]*powRe; sumIm+=coeffs[k]*powIm;
          const nRe=powRe*re-powIm*im; const nIm=powRe*im+powIm*re;
          powRe=nRe; powIm=nIm;
        }
        return [sumRe, sumIm];
      }
      default: return [NaN,NaN];
    }
  }

  function computeMaxError9(fname, rInner, rOuter, N, SAMPLES) {
    // Estimate max |f_exact - f_partial| on a circle of radius midR
    const midR = Math.sqrt(rInner * rOuter); // geometric mean
    let maxErr = 0;
    for(let k=0;k<SAMPLES;k++) {
      const theta = 2*Math.PI*k/SAMPLES;
      const re = midR*Math.cos(theta), im = midR*Math.sin(theta);
      const [er,ei] = evalExact9(fname, re, im);
      const [pr,pi] = evalPartial9(fname, re, im, N);
      if(!isFinite(er)||!isFinite(pr)) continue;
      const err = Math.sqrt((er-pr)**2+(ei-pi)**2);
      if(err>maxErr) maxErr=err;
    }
    return maxErr;
  }

  function hslToRgb9(h,s,l) {
    h=((h%1)+1)%1;
    const c=(1-Math.abs(2*l-1))*s,x=c*(1-Math.abs((h*6)%2-1)),m=l-c/2;
    let r=0,g=0,b=0;
    if(h<1/6){r=c;g=x;}else if(h<2/6){r=x;g=c;}else if(h<3/6){g=c;b=x;}
    else if(h<4/6){g=x;b=c;}else if(h<5/6){r=x;b=c;}else{r=c;b=x;}
    return [Math.round((r+m)*255),Math.round((g+m)*255),Math.round((b+m)*255)];
  }

  function toScr9(re,im) { return [CX+re*SCALE, CY-im*SCALE]; }

  function renderPanel9(fname, rInner, rOuter, N, usePartial) {
    const canvas=document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width=W; canvas.height=H;
    const ctx=canvas.getContext("2d");
    const img=ctx.createImageData(W,H); const data=img.data;

    for(let px=0;px<W;px++) {
      for(let py=0;py<H;py++) {
        const re=(px-CX)/SCALE, im=-(py-CY)/SCALE;
        const dist=Math.sqrt(re*re+im*im);
        const inAnnulus = dist > rInner && dist < rOuter;

        if(!inAnnulus) {
          const idx=(py*W+px)*4; data[idx]=210;data[idx+1]=210;data[idx+2]=210;data[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }

        const [wr,wi] = usePartial ? evalPartial9(fname,re,im,N) : evalExact9(fname,re,im);
        if(!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)||isNaN(wr)||Math.abs(wr)>1e6||Math.abs(wi)>1e6) {
          const idx=(py*W+px)*4; data[idx]=255;data[idx+1]=255;data[idx+2]=255;data[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const arg=Math.atan2(wi,wr), mag=Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue=(arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const brightness=0.5+0.35*Math.tanh(Math.log(mag+0.001)/2);
        const [r,g,b]=hslToRgb9(hue,0.8,brightness);
        const idx=(py*W+px)*4; data[idx]=r;data[idx+1]=g;data[idx+2]=b;data[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    ctx.putImageData(img,0,0);

    const [ox,oy]=toScr9(0,0);
    // Axes
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.4)"; ctx.lineWidth=0.8;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0,oy); ctx.lineTo(W,oy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox,0); ctx.lineTo(ox,H); ctx.stroke();

    // Inner barrier (blue)
    ctx.strokeStyle="#3b82f6"; ctx.lineWidth=2.5; ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox,oy,rInner*SCALE,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.stroke();
    // Inner label
    ctx.fillStyle="#3b82f6"; ctx.font="bold 9px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("inner singularity", ox+rInner*SCALE*0.6,oy-rInner*SCALE-4);
    ctx.fillText("barrier r="+rInner.toFixed(2), ox+rInner*SCALE*0.6, oy-rInner*SCALE+8);

    // Outer barrier (orange)
    ctx.strokeStyle="#f97316"; ctx.lineWidth=2.5;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox,oy,Math.min(rOuter*SCALE,W*0.72),0,2*Math.PI); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="#f97316"; ctx.font="bold 9px sans-serif";
    const angOuter = -0.5;
    const ox2=ox+Math.min(rOuter*SCALE,W*0.72)*Math.cos(angOuter), oy2=oy+Math.min(rOuter*SCALE,W*0.72)*Math.sin(angOuter);
    ctx.fillText("outer singularity", ox2+4, oy2-3);
    ctx.fillText("barrier R="+rOuter.toFixed(2), ox2+4, oy2+9);

    // Singularity markers
    const meta = funcMeta[fname];
    meta.sings.forEach(s => {
      const [sx,sy]=toScr9(s.re,s.im);
      ctx.strokeStyle="#dc2626"; ctx.lineWidth=2;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(sx-6,sy-6); ctx.lineTo(sx+6,sy+6); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(sx+6,sy-6); ctx.lineTo(sx-6,sy+6); ctx.stroke();
    });

    // Title
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(0,0,0,0.75)"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText(usePartial?`N=${N}-term partial sum`:"exact f(z)", 5, H-7);

    return canvas;
  }

  function renderLaurent9(fname, rInner, rOuter, N) {
    if(rOuter <= rInner + 0.01) rOuter = rInner + 0.15;
    const meta = funcMeta[fname];
    const isEssential = fname === "e^{1/z} (essential)";

    const panelsDiv = document.createElement("div");
    panelsDiv.style.cssText = "display:flex; gap:0.5rem; flex-wrap:wrap;";

    const exactCanvas = renderPanel9(fname, rInner, rOuter, N, false);
    const partialCanvas = renderPanel9(fname, rInner, rOuter, N, true);

    // Label wrappers
    function labeled(canvas, labelText) {
      const d = document.createElement("div");
      const lbl = document.createElement("div");
      lbl.style.cssText = "font-size:0.8em; font-weight:600; text-align:center; margin-bottom:2px; color:#374151;";
      lbl.textContent = labelText;
      d.appendChild(lbl); d.appendChild(canvas);
      return d;
    }

    panelsDiv.appendChild(labeled(exactCanvas, "Exact f(z) in annulus"));
    if(isEssential) panelsDiv.appendChild(labeled(partialCanvas, `Partial sum (N=${N} terms of e^{1/z})`));

    const infoDiv = document.createElement("div");
    infoDiv.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.85em;";

    let ppDesc = meta.ppTerms === Infinity
      ? `<strong style="color:#dc2626">∞ principal-part terms</strong> — essential singularity`
      : `<strong>${meta.ppTerms}</strong> principal-part term${meta.ppTerms===1?"":"s"}`;

    let errStr = "";
    if(isEssential) {
      const maxErr = computeMaxError9(fname, rInner, rOuter, N, 64);
      errStr = `<div style="margin-top:0.3rem;color:#374151;"><strong>Max error on midpoint circle:</strong> ${maxErr.toExponential(3)}</div>`;
    }

    infoDiv.innerHTML = `
      <div><strong>Singularity type:</strong> <span style="color:#1e40af">${meta.singType}</span></div>
      <div><strong>Principal part:</strong> ${ppDesc}</div>
      <div><strong>Convergence annulus:</strong> ${rInner.toFixed(3)} &lt; |z| &lt; ${rOuter.toFixed(2)} — shown in colour; grey = outside</div>
      ${errStr}
    `;

    const wrap = document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(panelsDiv); wrap.appendChild(infoDiv);
    return wrap;
  }

  const container=document.createElement("div");
  container.style.cssText="border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const title9=document.createElement("div");
  title9.style.cssText="font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  title9.textContent="Laurent annulus: convergence barriers and singularity type";
  container.appendChild(title9);
  container.appendChild(funcSel9);
  container.appendChild(rInnerSl);
  container.appendChild(rOuterSl);
  container.appendChild(nTermsSl);

  const vizDiv9=document.createElement("div");
  container.appendChild(vizDiv9);

  const note9=document.createElement("div");
  note9.style.cssText="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  note9.textContent="Domain colouring (hue = arg f, brightness = log|f|) shown only inside the annulus r < |z| < R. Blue circle = inner singularity barrier; orange circle = outer singularity barrier. For e^{1/z}, the right panel shows the N-term partial sum alongside exact f(z). Red × marks singularities.";
  container.appendChild(note9);

  function update9() {
    let rI = parseFloat(rInnerSl.value), rO = parseFloat(rOuterSl.value);
    if(rO <= rI + 0.01) rO = rI + 0.15;
    vizDiv9.innerHTML="";
    vizDiv9.appendChild(renderLaurent9(funcSel9.value, rI, rO, parseInt(nTermsSl.value)));
  }
  funcSel9.addEventListener("input", update9);
  rInnerSl.addEventListener("input", update9);
  rOuterSl.addEventListener("input", update9);
  nTermsSl.addEventListener("input", update9);
  update9();

  return container;
}
```

**Computing Laurent series in practice.** For functions that are products, quotients, or compositions of known series, it is usually more efficient to manipulate the known Taylor series directly rather than computing coefficients by integration.

**Example.** $\sin z / z^3$ near $z = 0$:

$$\frac{\sin z}{z^3} = \frac{1}{z^3}\left(z - \frac{z^3}{6} + \frac{z^5}{120} - \cdots\right) = \frac{1}{z^2} - \frac{1}{6} + \frac{z^2}{120} - \cdots$$

The principal part has only one negative-power term, $1/z^2$.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // Laurent coefficient spectrum — missed opportunity 4
  // Bar chart of c_n for n=−6..+4; red bars = principal part (n<0), blue = analytic (n≥0)
  // Right panel: domain colouring built by adding k principal-part terms one by one
  const W2 = 320, H2 = 280, CX2 = W2/2, CY2 = H2/2, SCALE2 = 55;

  const funcSelSpec = Inputs.select([
    "1/z(z-1)  [2 pp terms]",
    "e^{1/z}    [∞ pp terms]",
    "sin(z)/z   [0 pp terms — removable]",
    "1/z²       [1 pp term — order-2 pole]"
  ], { value: "1/z(z-1)  [2 pp terms]", label: "f(z)" });

  const kSlider = Inputs.range([0, 6], { value: 0, step: 1, label: "Principal-part terms added (k)" });

  // Laurent coefficients c_n for n = -6..+4 (index 0 = n=-6)
  function getLaurentCoeffs(fname) {
    // Returns array of {n, c} for n=-6..4
    const result = [];
    for(let n=-6; n<=4; n++) {
      let c = 0;
      if(fname.startsWith("1/z(z-1)")) {
        // 1/(z(z-1)) = -1/z - 1 - z - z^2 - ... for |z|<1
        if(n===-1) c=-1;
        else if(n>=0) c=-1;
        else c=0;
      } else if(fname.startsWith("e^{1/z}")) {
        // e^{1/z} = sum_{k=0}^∞ (1/z)^k / k! = sum_{k=0}^∞ z^{-k} / k!
        if(n<=0) c = 1/factorial(-n);
        else c = 0;
      } else if(fname.startsWith("sin(z)/z")) {
        // sin(z)/z = 1 - z²/6 + z⁴/120 - ...
        if(n===0) c=1; else if(n===2) c=-1/6; else if(n===4) c=1/120; else c=0;
      } else if(fname.startsWith("1/z²")) {
        if(n===-2) c=1; else c=0;
      }
      result.push({n, c});
    }
    return result;
  }

  function factorial(k) {
    if(k<=0) return 1; let f=1; for(let i=2;i<=k;i++) f*=i; return f;
  }

  // Evaluate partial sum using k principal-part terms
  function evalKTerms(fname, re, im, k) {
    const coeffs = getLaurentCoeffs(fname);
    // Principal-part coefficients: n < 0, sorted from most-negative to -1
    const ppCoeffs = coeffs.filter(c=>c.n<0&&c.c!==0).sort((a,b)=>a.n-b.n);
    const analyticCoeffs = coeffs.filter(c=>c.n>=0);
    // Take first k principal-part terms (smallest n first)
    const activeCoeffs = [
      ...ppCoeffs.slice(0, k),
      ...analyticCoeffs
    ];
    const d2 = re*re+im*im; if(d2<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
    let sumRe=0, sumIm=0;
    for(const {n, c} of activeCoeffs) {
      if(c===0) continue;
      // z^n = r^n * e^{i*n*theta}
      const r = Math.sqrt(d2);
      const theta = Math.atan2(im, re);
      const rn = Math.pow(r, n);
      if(!isFinite(rn)) continue;
      sumRe += c * rn * Math.cos(n*theta);
      sumIm += c * rn * Math.sin(n*theta);
    }
    return [sumRe, sumIm];
  }

  function hslToRgbSpec(h,s,l) {
    h=((h%1)+1)%1;
    const c=(1-Math.abs(2*l-1))*s,x=c*(1-Math.abs((h*6)%2-1)),m=l-c/2;
    let r=0,g=0,b=0;
    if(h<1/6){r=c;g=x;}else if(h<2/6){r=x;g=c;}else if(h<3/6){g=c;b=x;}
    else if(h<4/6){g=x;b=c;}else if(h<5/6){r=x;b=c;}else{r=c;b=x;}
    return [Math.round((r+m)*255),Math.round((g+m)*255),Math.round((b+m)*255)];
  }

  function renderSpectrum(fname, k) {
    const coeffs = getLaurentCoeffs(fname);
    const ppCoeffs = coeffs.filter(c=>c.n<0&&c.c!==0).sort((a,b)=>a.n-b.n);
    const kCapped = Math.min(k, ppCoeffs.length);

    // --- Bar chart ---
    const BW = 380, BH = 200;
    const barCanvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    barCanvas.width = BW; barCanvas.height = BH;
    const bctx = barCanvas.getContext("2d");
    bctx.fillStyle="#f9fafb";
    bctx.fillRect(0,0,BW,BH);

    const nVals = coeffs.map(c=>c.n);
    const n0 = nVals[0], n1 = nVals[nVals.length-1];
    const totalBars = n1-n0+1;
    const barW = Math.floor((BW-40) / totalBars) - 2;
    const xOff = 30;
    const zeroY = BH - 35;
    const maxAbs = Math.max(...coeffs.map(c=>Math.abs(c.c)), 0.01);
    const scaleY = (BH - 55) / maxAbs;

    // Zero line
    bctx.strokeStyle="#9ca3af"; bctx.lineWidth=1;
    bctx.beginPath(); bctx.moveTo(xOff, zeroY); bctx.lineTo(BW-10, zeroY); bctx.stroke();

    coeffs.forEach(({n,c}) => {
      const barIdx = n - n0;
      const x = xOff + barIdx * (barW+2) + 1;
      const h = Math.abs(c) * scaleY;
      const y = c >= 0 ? zeroY - h : zeroY;

      // Highlight active terms
      const isPP = n < 0;
      const ppIdx = ppCoeffs.findIndex(p=>p.n===n);
      const isActive = isPP ? (ppIdx >= 0 && ppIdx < kCapped) : true;
      const isAnalytic = n >= 0;

      bctx.fillStyle = isPP
        ? (isActive ? "#dc2626" : "rgba(220,38,38,0.25)")
        : (c!==0 ? "#3b82f6" : "#e5e7eb");
      bctx.fillRect(x, y, barW, Math.max(h, 1));

      // n label
      bctx.fillStyle = "#374151"; bctx.font="9px sans-serif"; bctx.textAlign="center";
      bctx.fillText(n.toString(), x+barW/2, zeroY+12);

      // c value for non-zero
      if(Math.abs(c)>0.001) {
        bctx.fillStyle = isPP ? (isActive?"#dc2626":"#f87171") : "#3b82f6";
        bctx.font="8px sans-serif";
        const valStr = Number.isInteger(c)?c.toString():c.toFixed(3);
        bctx.fillText(valStr, x+barW/2, c>=0 ? zeroY-h-3 : zeroY+h+20);
      }
    });
    bctx.textAlign="left";

    // Axis label
    bctx.fillStyle="#374151"; bctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    bctx.fillText("n", BW-15, zeroY+3);
    bctx.fillStyle="#dc2626"; bctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    bctx.fillText("red = principal part (n<0)", 30, 14);
    bctx.fillStyle="#3b82f6";
    bctx.fillText("blue = analytic part (n≥0)", 220, 14);

    // --- Domain colouring panel ---
    const dcCanvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    dcCanvas.width=W2; dcCanvas.height=H2;
    const dctx=dcCanvas.getContext("2d");
    const img2=dctx.createImageData(W2,H2); const dd=img2.data;

    for(let px=0;px<W2;px++) {
      for(let py=0;py<H2;py++) {
        const re=(px-CX2)/SCALE2, im=-(py-CY2)/SCALE2;
        const [wr,wi]=evalKTerms(fname,re,im,kCapped);
        if(!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)||isNaN(wr)||Math.abs(wr)>1e5) {
          const idx=(py*W2+px)*4; dd[idx]=255;dd[idx+1]=255;dd[idx+2]=255;dd[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const arg=Math.atan2(wi,wr), mag=Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue=(arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const brightness=0.5+0.35*Math.tanh(Math.log(mag+0.001)/2);
        const [r,g,b]=hslToRgbSpec(hue,0.8,brightness);
        const idx=(py*W2+px)*4; dd[idx]=r;dd[idx+1]=g;dd[idx+2]=b;dd[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    dctx.putImageData(img2,0,0);

    // Axes on dc panel
    const [dcox,dcoy]=[CX2,CY2];
    dctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.4)"; dctx.lineWidth=0.8;
    dctx.beginPath(); dctx.moveTo(0,dcoy); dctx.lineTo(W2,dcoy); dctx.stroke();
    dctx.beginPath(); dctx.moveTo(dcox,0); dctx.lineTo(dcox,H2); dctx.stroke();
    dctx.fillStyle="rgba(0,0,0,0.7)"; dctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    dctx.fillText(`${kCapped} pp term${kCapped===1?"":"s"} added`, 5, H2-7);

    const stepLabel = document.createElement("div");
    stepLabel.style.cssText="text-align:center; font-size:0.85em; color:#374151; margin:0.25rem 0;";
    stepLabel.textContent = kCapped === 0
      ? "Step 0: analytic part only (no principal-part terms)"
      : `Step ${kCapped}: adding c_{${ppCoeffs[kCapped-1]?.n}} term to the reconstruction`;

    const panelDiv = document.createElement("div");
    panelDiv.style.cssText="display:flex; gap:0.5rem; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:flex-start;";
    panelDiv.appendChild(barCanvas); panelDiv.appendChild(dcCanvas);

    const wrap = document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(panelDiv);
    wrap.appendChild(stepLabel);
    return wrap;
  }

  const container2 = document.createElement("div");
  container2.style.cssText="border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const title2 = document.createElement("div");
  title2.style.cssText="font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  title2.textContent="Laurent coefficient spectrum: principal part vs analytic part";
  container2.appendChild(title2);
  container2.appendChild(funcSelSpec);
  container2.appendChild(kSlider);
  const vizDiv2 = document.createElement("div");
  container2.appendChild(vizDiv2);
  const note2 = document.createElement("div");
  note2.style.cssText="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  note2.textContent="Bar chart: red = principal-part coefficients (n<0), blue = analytic-part coefficients (n≥0). Slider adds principal-part terms one at a time; domain colouring in right panel updates. Bright red bars are active, faded red bars are not yet included.";
  container2.appendChild(note2);

  function updateSpec() {
    vizDiv2.innerHTML="";
    vizDiv2.appendChild(renderSpectrum(funcSelSpec.value, parseInt(kSlider.value)));
  }
  funcSelSpec.addEventListener("input", updateSpec);
  kSlider.addEventListener("input", updateSpec);
  updateSpec();

  return container2;
}
```

## Classification of isolated singularities

An **isolated singularity** of $f$ at $z_0$ is a point where $f$ is not analytic but is analytic in some punctured disk $0 < |z - z_0| < \delta$. The Laurent series reveals the type:

**Removable singularity.** The principal part is absent (no negative-power terms). $f$ can be assigned a value at $z_0$ to make it analytic. Example: $\sin z / z$ at $z = 0$ — the Laurent series is $1 - z^2/6 + \cdots$, which extends continuously to $z = 0$ with value 1.

**Pole of order $m$.** The principal part has exactly $m$ terms:
$$f(z) = \frac{c_{-m}}{(z-z_0)^m} + \cdots + \frac{c_{-1}}{z-z_0} + c_0 + c_1(z-z_0) + \cdots, \quad c_{-m} \neq 0$$
$|f(z)| \to \infty$ as $z \to z_0$. A **simple pole** is a pole of order 1.

**Essential singularity.** The principal part has infinitely many terms. The behaviour near $z_0$ has no limit — finite or infinite. Example: $e^{1/z}$ at $z = 0$. Approach the origin along the positive real axis and $e^{1/z} \to +\infty$; along the negative real axis, $e^{1/z} \to 0$; along the imaginary axis, $e^{1/z}$ spirals and oscillates. In any small neighbourhood of 0, the function takes every complex value (with at most one exception).

<!-- VIZ: Singularity classification visualiser — domain colouring zoom. A function selector offers three functions, each with an isolated singularity at z = 0: "sin(z)/z (removable)", "1/z (simple pole)", "1/z² (order-2 pole)", "e^{1/z} (essential)". The main panel shows domain colouring (hue = arg f, brightness = log|f|) of the selected function over a square region. A zoom slider shrinks the viewport towards the origin: range 3 to 0.01 in log scale. A singularity-type label updates live. For the removable singularity, the domain colouring stays smooth and bounded as you zoom in — the function is extending continuously. For the pole, brightness intensifies (blossoms white) and the hue wheel winds once (simple) or twice (order 2) around the origin. For the essential singularity, zooming in reveals ever-finer multi-coloured oscillations with no limiting pattern — Picard's theorem made visible: every colour (every value) appears near the origin. An annotation panel below the plot states the singularity type and the number of hue-winding revolutions counted around a small circle. Series palette: consistent with Chapter 1 and 2 domain-colouring vocabulary. This is the most visually striking moment of the complex analysis section — essential singularities are genuinely extreme and should look it. -->


<!-- STUDENT: Picard's theorem is cited but not introduced — the reader has not seen it before. For the purposes of this chapter, the claim "behaviour near an essential singularity is wild" is all that's needed; invoking a named theorem that appears nowhere else in the series may feel like a reference to unknown material. If Picard's theorem is not covered elsewhere, consider replacing it with a brief concrete illustration (e.g. noting that e^{1/z} oscillates arbitrarily fast near 0). -->

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // Singularity classifier — log-scale zoom, domain colouring, 4 singularity types
  const W_SC = 420, H_SC = 380, CX_SC = W_SC/2, CY_SC = H_SC/2;

  const funcSelSC = Inputs.select([
    "sin(z)/z   — removable",
    "1/z        — simple pole (order 1)",
    "1/z²       — order-2 pole",
    "e^{1/z}    — essential singularity"
  ], { value: "sin(z)/z   — removable", label: "Singularity type" });

  // Zoom: log scale, viewport half-width from 2 down to 0.002
  const zoomSl = Inputs.range([Math.log10(0.002), Math.log10(2)], {
    value: Math.log10(0.5), step: 0.02, label: "log₁₀(viewport half-width)"
  });

  function evalSC(fname, re, im) {
    if(fname.startsWith("sin(z)/z")) {
      // sin(z)/z: at z=0 value is 1 (removable singularity)
      const r2=re*re+im*im; if(r2<1e-12) return [1,0];
      // sin(z) = sin(x)cosh(y) + i cos(x)sinh(y)
      const sr=Math.sin(re)*Math.cosh(im), si=Math.cos(re)*Math.sinh(im);
      const d=r2; // divide by z: (sr+isi)/(re+iim)
      return [(sr*re+si*im)/d, (si*re-sr*im)/d];
    }
    if(fname.startsWith("1/z ")) {
      const d=re*re+im*im; if(d<1e-12) return [NaN,NaN];
      return [re/d, -im/d];
    }
    if(fname.startsWith("1/z²")) {
      const d=re*re+im*im; if(d<1e-12) return [NaN,NaN];
      const d2=d*d;
      return [(re*re-im*im)/d2, -2*re*im/d2];
    }
    if(fname.startsWith("e^{1/z}")) {
      const d=re*re+im*im; if(d<1e-12) return [NaN,NaN];
      const invRe=re/d, invIm=-im/d;
      return [Math.exp(invRe)*Math.cos(invIm), Math.exp(invRe)*Math.sin(invIm)];
    }
    return [1,0];
  }

  function hslToRgbSC(h,s,l) {
    h=((h%1)+1)%1;
    const c=(1-Math.abs(2*l-1))*s,x=c*(1-Math.abs((h*6)%2-1)),m=l-c/2;
    let r=0,g=0,b=0;
    if(h<1/6){r=c;g=x;}else if(h<2/6){r=x;g=c;}else if(h<3/6){g=c;b=x;}
    else if(h<4/6){g=x;b=c;}else if(h<5/6){r=x;b=c;}else{r=c;b=x;}
    return [Math.round((r+m)*255),Math.round((g+m)*255),Math.round((b+m)*255)];
  }

  function renderSC(fname, logHalfWidth) {
    const halfW = Math.pow(10, logHalfWidth);
    const scale = W_SC / (2 * halfW);

    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width = W_SC; canvas.height = H_SC;
    const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
    const img = ctx.createImageData(W_SC, H_SC); const data = img.data;

    for(let px=0; px<W_SC; px++) {
      for(let py=0; py<H_SC; py++) {
        const re = (px - CX_SC) / scale;
        const im = -(py - CY_SC) / scale;
        const [wr,wi] = evalSC(fname, re, im);
        if(!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)||isNaN(wr)) {
          const idx=(py*W_SC+px)*4; data[idx]=255;data[idx+1]=255;data[idx+2]=255;data[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const arg=Math.atan2(wi,wr), mag=Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue=(arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const brightness=0.5+0.35*Math.tanh(Math.log(mag+0.001)/2);
        const [r,g,b]=hslToRgbSC(hue,0.8,brightness);
        const idx=(py*W_SC+px)*4; data[idx]=r;data[idx+1]=g;data[idx+2]=b;data[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    ctx.putImageData(img,0,0);

    // Axes
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.5)"; ctx.lineWidth=0.8;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0,H_SC/2); ctx.lineTo(W_SC,H_SC/2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(W_SC/2,0); ctx.lineTo(W_SC/2,H_SC); ctx.stroke();

    // Scale indicator
    const tickPx = scale; // 1 unit in pixels
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.85)"; ctx.lineWidth=2;
    const ty = H_SC-18;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(W_SC/2-tickPx/2,ty); ctx.lineTo(W_SC/2+tickPx/2,ty); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.9)"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign="center";
    ctx.fillText(`|z| = ${halfW < 0.01 ? halfW.toExponential(2) : halfW.toFixed(4)}`, W_SC/2, ty-4);
    ctx.fillText("← 1 unit →", W_SC/2, ty+12);
    ctx.textAlign="left";

    // Type annotation
    const isEss = fname.startsWith("e^{1/z}");
    const isRem = fname.startsWith("sin(z)/z");
    let typeColor = isEss ? "#f97316" : isRem ? "#059669" : "#3b82f6";
    let typeLabel = isEss ? "Essential singularity" : isRem ? "Removable singularity" : fname.startsWith("1/z²") ? "Pole of order 2" : "Simple pole (order 1)";

    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(0,0,0,0.7)";
    ctx.fillRect(0,0,W_SC,22);
    ctx.fillStyle=typeColor; ctx.font="bold 11px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText(typeLabel, 6, 15);

    // Persistent annotation for essential singularity at fine zoom
    const infoDiv = document.createElement("div");
    infoDiv.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.4rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.86em; padding:0.4rem 0.6rem; border-radius:4px;";

    if(isEss && halfW < 0.1) {
      infoDiv.style.background="#fff7ed";
      infoDiv.style.border="1px solid #fed7aa";
      infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong style="color:#f97316">No pattern emerges — every colour appears in every neighbourhood.</strong> As you zoom in on the essential singularity at z=0, the domain colouring continues to show all hues (all argument values) densely packed, with no limiting structure. This is what makes an essential singularity different from every other type.`;
    } else if(isRem) {
      infoDiv.style.background="#f0fdf4";
      infoDiv.style.border="1px solid #bbf7d0";
      infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong style="color:#059669">Removable singularity:</strong> as you zoom in, the domain colouring stabilises — it looks like the colouring of an analytic function. The function extends continuously to z=0 (value: 1 for sin(z)/z). No winding of the hue wheel around the origin.`;
    } else if(fname.startsWith("1/z²")) {
      infoDiv.style.background="#eff6ff";
      infoDiv.style.border="1px solid #bfdbfe";
      infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong style="color:#3b82f6">Pole of order 2:</strong> the hue wheel winds <strong>twice</strong> around the origin. Brightness intensifies (blooms white) as you zoom in — |f(z)| → ∞. The origin is a zero of the conformal image; the order-2 pole shows two full colour cycles per small circle.`;
    } else {
      infoDiv.style.background="#eff6ff";
      infoDiv.style.border="1px solid #bfdbfe";
      infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong style="color:#3b82f6">Simple pole (order 1):</strong> the hue wheel winds <strong>once</strong> around the origin. Brightness blooms white at the centre. Winding number = order of the pole.`;
    }

    const wrap = document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(canvas); wrap.appendChild(infoDiv);
    return wrap;
  }

  const containerSC = document.createElement("div");
  containerSC.style.cssText = "border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const titleSC = document.createElement("div");
  titleSC.style.cssText = "font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  titleSC.textContent = "Singularity classifier: zoom in on isolated singularities";
  containerSC.appendChild(titleSC);
  containerSC.appendChild(funcSelSC);
  containerSC.appendChild(zoomSl);
  const vizDivSC = document.createElement("div");
  containerSC.appendChild(vizDivSC);
  const noteSC = document.createElement("div");
  noteSC.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  noteSC.textContent = "Domain colouring: hue = arg f, brightness = log|f| — identical to Ch1/Ch2. Zoom slider ranges from viewport half-width 2 down to 0.002. For a removable singularity, the colouring stays smooth; for a pole of order m, the hue wheel winds m times; for an essential singularity, every colour appears in every neighbourhood with no limiting pattern.";
  containerSC.appendChild(noteSC);

  function updateSC() {
    vizDivSC.innerHTML = "";
    vizDivSC.appendChild(renderSC(funcSelSC.value, parseFloat(zoomSl.value)));
  }
  funcSelSC.addEventListener("input", updateSC);
  zoomSl.addEventListener("input", updateSC);
  updateSC();

  return containerSC;
}
```

## Residues

The **residue** of $f$ at an isolated singularity $z_0$ is the Laurent coefficient $c_{-1}$:

$$\text{Res}[f, z_0] = c_{-1}$$

**Why it matters.** Chapter 2 proved by direct parametrisation that $\oint_{|z-z_0|=r}(z-z_0)^n\,dz = 2\pi i$ when $n = -1$ and $= 0$ for every other integer $n$. (The same substitution $z = z_0 + re^{i\theta}$ works for all integers, not just $n = 0$ as computed there.) So when the Laurent series is integrated term by term around a small circle enclosing $z_0$, every term vanishes except the $c_{-1}$ term:
$$\oint_C \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} c_n(z-z_0)^n\,dz = c_{-1}\cdot 2\pi i$$

<!-- STUDENT: This is the key conceptual step of the chapter, but it relies on the result from Chapter 2 (§ A fundamental example) that was proved only for n = 0. Here it is asserted for all integers n. A brief callback — "as shown in Chapter 2 for n = 0, and provable similarly for all integers n" — would connect the two chapters and confirm the reader isn't expected to prove this themselves. -->

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // Why only c₋₁ survives — missed opportunity 2
  // Circle with z = r e^{iθ} travelling; integer slider n; arrows show integrand contribution
  // Right panel: accumulated contour integral as curve in C-plane — closes to 0 for n≠-1, to 2πi for n=-1

  const W_C1 = 320, H_C1 = 300, CX_C1 = W_C1/2, CY_C1 = H_C1/2, SC_C1 = 90;
  const W_C2 = 300, H_C2 = 300, CX_C2 = W_C2/2, CY_C2 = H_C2/2;

  const nSlider = Inputs.range([-4, 3], { value: -1, step: 1, label: "Power n in z^n" });
  const tSlider = Inputs.range([0, 1], { value: 0, step: 0.004, label: "Progress t (0→1 = full circle)" });

  const rCircle = 1.0; // circle radius |z| = r = 1

  // Integral of z^n dz around circle of radius r, from 0 to 2πt
  // z = r e^{iθ}, dz = ir e^{iθ} dθ
  // integrand = r^n e^{inθ} * ir e^{iθ} = i r^{n+1} e^{i(n+1)θ}
  function computeIntegralC1(n, t, STEPS) {
    const dtheta = 2*Math.PI*t / Math.max(STEPS,1);
    let sumRe=0, sumIm=0;
    for(let k=0;k<STEPS;k++) {
      const theta = 2*Math.PI * k*t / STEPS;
      const dthE = 2*Math.PI * t / STEPS;
      // integrand z^n dz at midpoint
      const thM = theta + dthE/2;
      const r = rCircle;
      // z^n = r^n e^{inθ}
      const znRe = Math.pow(r,n)*Math.cos(n*thM);
      const znIm = Math.pow(r,n)*Math.sin(n*thM);
      // dz = ir e^{iθ} dθ = r(-sin θ + i cos θ) dθ
      const dzRe = -r*Math.sin(thM)*dthE;
      const dzIm =  r*Math.cos(thM)*dthE;
      sumRe += znRe*dzRe - znIm*dzIm;
      sumIm += znRe*dzIm + znIm*dzRe;
    }
    return [sumRe, sumIm];
  }

  function toScrC1(re,im) { return [CX_C1+re*SC_C1, CY_C1-im*SC_C1]; }
  function toScrC2(re,im) { // C2: scale to fit result; n=-1 gives 2πi ~ 6.28
    const s2 = H_C2*0.35 / (2*Math.PI);
    return [CX_C2+re*s2, CY_C2-im*s2];
  }

  function renderC1(n, tVal) {
    const STEPS = 200;
    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width=W_C1; canvas.height=H_C1;
    const ctx=canvas.getContext("2d");
    ctx.fillStyle="#fafafa"; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W_C1,H_C1);

    // Grid
    ctx.strokeStyle="#e5e7eb"; ctx.lineWidth=0.5;
    for(let i=-2;i<=2;i++) {
      const [lx]=toScrC1(i,0); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(lx,0); ctx.lineTo(lx,H_C1); ctx.stroke();
      const [,ly]=toScrC1(0,i); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0,ly); ctx.lineTo(W_C1,ly); ctx.stroke();
    }

    // Axes
    const [ox,oy]=toScrC1(0,0);
    ctx.strokeStyle="#9ca3af"; ctx.lineWidth=1;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0,oy); ctx.lineTo(W_C1,oy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox,0); ctx.lineTo(ox,H_C1); ctx.stroke();

    // Full circle outline
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(156,163,175,0.4)"; ctx.lineWidth=1.5; ctx.setLineDash([4,3]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox,oy,rCircle*SC_C1,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);

    // Traced portion of circle (orange for n=-1, blue otherwise)
    const traceColor = n===-1 ? "#f97316" : "#3b82f6";
    ctx.strokeStyle=traceColor; ctx.lineWidth=2.5;
    ctx.beginPath();
    for(let k=0;k<=STEPS;k++) {
      const theta = 2*Math.PI*(k/STEPS)*tVal;
      const [px,py]=toScrC1(rCircle*Math.cos(theta), rCircle*Math.sin(theta));
      k===0?ctx.moveTo(px,py):ctx.lineTo(px,py);
    }
    ctx.stroke();

    // Arrows showing integrand direction at a few points along the traced arc
    const arrowCount = 8;
    for(let a=0;a<arrowCount;a++) {
      const frac = (a+0.5)/arrowCount;
      if(frac >= tVal && tVal < 0.98) continue;
      const theta = 2*Math.PI*frac;
      const [zx,zy] = [rCircle*Math.cos(theta), rCircle*Math.sin(theta)];
      // Integrand contribution direction: z^n * dz (dz direction = tangent = i*z/r)
      // direction of z^n * dz at this point
      const argZn = n * theta;
      const argDz = theta + Math.PI/2; // tangent direction
      const argContrib = argZn + argDz;
      const arrowLen = 0.28;
      const [ax1,ay1]=toScrC1(zx,zy);
      const ax2=ax1+arrowLen*SC_C1*Math.cos(argContrib);
      const ay2=ay1-arrowLen*SC_C1*Math.sin(argContrib);
      ctx.strokeStyle=n===-1?"#f97316":"rgba(59,130,246,0.7)"; ctx.lineWidth=1.5;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ax1,ay1); ctx.lineTo(ax2,ay2); ctx.stroke();
      // Arrowhead
      const headLen=7, headAngle=0.4;
      const dir=Math.atan2(ay1-ay2,ax2-ax1);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(ax2,ay2);
      ctx.lineTo(ax2-headLen*Math.cos(dir-headAngle), ay2+headLen*Math.sin(dir-headAngle));
      ctx.moveTo(ax2,ay2);
      ctx.lineTo(ax2-headLen*Math.cos(dir+headAngle), ay2+headLen*Math.sin(dir+headAngle));
      ctx.stroke();
    }

    // Current point z = re^{iθ}
    const thetaNow = 2*Math.PI*tVal;
    const [cpx,cpy]=toScrC1(rCircle*Math.cos(thetaNow), rCircle*Math.sin(thetaNow));
    ctx.fillStyle=traceColor; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cpx,cpy,6,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle="#fff"; ctx.lineWidth=1.5; ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="#374151"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText(`z = e^{iθ}`, cpx+8, cpy-4);

    // Origin mark
    ctx.fillStyle="#374151"; ctx.font="9px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("0", ox+4, oy-4);

    // Title
    ctx.fillStyle="#374151"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif";
    const nLabel = n>=0?`+${n}`:n.toString();
    ctx.fillText(`Integrand: z^{${nLabel}} dz on |z|=1`, 5, 14);

    return canvas;
  }

  function renderC2(n, tVal) {
    const STEPS = 200;
    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width=W_C2; canvas.height=H_C2;
    const ctx=canvas.getContext("2d");
    ctx.fillStyle="#fafafa"; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W_C2,H_C2);

    // Axes
    const [ox,oy]=toScrC2(0,0);
    ctx.strokeStyle="#9ca3af"; ctx.lineWidth=1;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0,oy); ctx.lineTo(W_C2,oy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox,0); ctx.lineTo(ox,H_C2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="#374151"; ctx.font="9px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("Re", W_C2-20,oy-3); ctx.fillText("Im", ox+3,10);

    // Mark 2πi on Im axis for n=-1
    if(n===-1) {
      const [,tpiY]=toScrC2(0,2*Math.PI);
      ctx.strokeStyle="#fbbf24"; ctx.lineWidth=1; ctx.setLineDash([3,2]);
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox-5,tpiY); ctx.lineTo(ox+5,tpiY); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
      ctx.fillStyle="#fbbf24"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
      ctx.fillText("2πi", ox+6, tpiY+4);
    }

    // Accumulated integral curve up to t
    const curveColor = n===-1?"#f97316":"#3b82f6";
    ctx.strokeStyle=curveColor; ctx.lineWidth=2;
    ctx.beginPath();
    for(let k=0;k<=STEPS;k++) {
      const tFrac = k/STEPS;
      if(tFrac > tVal + 0.001) break;
      const [ir,ii] = computeIntegralC1(n, tFrac, 80);
      const [px,py] = toScrC2(ir,ii);
      k===0?ctx.moveTo(px,py):ctx.lineTo(px,py);
    }
    ctx.stroke();

    // Current accumulated value
    const [curRe, curIm] = computeIntegralC1(n, tVal, 80);
    const [cpx,cpy]=toScrC2(curRe,curIm);
    ctx.fillStyle=curveColor; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cpx,cpy,5,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.fill();

    // Final value annotation
    if(tVal > 0.97) {
      const [fRe, fIm] = computeIntegralC1(n, 1, 200);
      const closed = Math.sqrt(fRe*fRe+fIm*fIm) < 0.1;
      if(n===-1) {
        ctx.fillStyle="#f97316"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif";
        ctx.fillText("→ 2πi ✓", cpx+8, cpy-4);
      } else {
        ctx.fillStyle="#3b82f6"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif";
        ctx.fillText("→ 0", cpx+8, cpy-4);
      }
    }

    // n=-1 gold highlight box
    if(n===-1) {
      ctx.fillStyle="rgba(251,191,36,0.15)"; ctx.fillRect(ox-60,0,120,H_C2);
    }

    ctx.fillStyle="#374151"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("∮ z^n dz (accumulating)", 4, 14);
    ctx.fillStyle=n===-1?"#f97316":"#374151"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    const resultLabel = n===-1 ? "n = −1: integral → 2πi" : `n = ${n}: integral → 0`;
    ctx.fillText(resultLabel, 4, H_C2-7);

    return canvas;
  }

  function renderC1C2(n, tVal) {
    const c1 = renderC1(n, tVal);
    const c2 = renderC2(n, tVal);
    const panelDiv = document.createElement("div");
    panelDiv.style.cssText = "display:flex; gap:0.5rem; flex-wrap:wrap;";

    function labeled2(canvas, lbl) {
      const d=document.createElement("div");
      const l=document.createElement("div");
      l.style.cssText="font-size:0.8em;font-weight:600;text-align:center;margin-bottom:2px;color:#374151;";
      l.textContent=lbl; d.appendChild(l); d.appendChild(canvas); return d;
    }

    panelDiv.appendChild(labeled2(c1, "Circle: z = e^{iθ}, arrows = integrand direction"));
    panelDiv.appendChild(labeled2(c2, "Accumulated integral in C"));

    const nLabel = n>=0?`+${n}`:n.toString();
    const infoDiv = document.createElement("div");
    infoDiv.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.4rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.86em;";

    if(n===-1) {
      infoDiv.style.cssText += "background:#fff7ed; border:1px solid #fed7aa; border-radius:4px; padding:0.35rem 0.6rem;";
      infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong style="color:#f97316">n = −1 (the residue term):</strong> the integrand z<sup>−1</sup> dz keeps accumulating in the <em>same direction</em> all around the circle — the curve in the right panel spirals up to 2πi without cancellation. This is why the coefficient c<sub>−1</sub> is the only one that survives when the Laurent series is integrated.`;
    } else {
      infoDiv.style.cssText += "background:#eff6ff; border:1px solid #bfdbfe; border-radius:4px; padding:0.35rem 0.6rem;";
      infoDiv.innerHTML = `<strong style="color:#3b82f6">n = ${nLabel}:</strong> the integrand contributions rotate around the origin — by the time the circle closes, they cancel exactly and the accumulated integral returns to 0. Every term in the Laurent series except c<sub>−1</sub> contributes zero to the contour integral.`;
    }

    const wrap = document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(panelDiv); wrap.appendChild(infoDiv);
    return wrap;
  }

  const containerC1 = document.createElement("div");
  containerC1.style.cssText = "border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const titleC1 = document.createElement("div");
  titleC1.style.cssText = "font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  titleC1.textContent = "Why only c₋₁ survives: ∮ zⁿ dz = 2πi if n = −1, else 0";
  containerC1.appendChild(titleC1);
  containerC1.appendChild(nSlider);
  containerC1.appendChild(tSlider);
  const vizDivC1 = document.createElement("div");
  containerC1.appendChild(vizDivC1);
  const noteC1 = document.createElement("div");
  noteC1.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  noteC1.textContent = "Left: the contour |z|=1 with arrows showing the direction of z^n dz at each point. Right: the accumulated contour integral as a curve in the complex plane. For n≠−1, the curve closes back on 0. For n=−1 (highlighted in orange), it spirals up to 2πi — the only non-cancelling term.";
  containerC1.appendChild(noteC1);

  function updateC1() {
    vizDivC1.innerHTML="";
    vizDivC1.appendChild(renderC1C2(parseInt(nSlider.value), parseFloat(tSlider.value)));
  }
  nSlider.addEventListener("input", updateC1);
  tSlider.addEventListener("input", updateC1);
  updateC1();

  return containerC1;
}
```

### Computing residues

**At a simple pole:** $\text{Res}[f, z_0] = \lim_{z \to z_0}(z-z_0)f(z)$.

**At a simple pole of $p/q$ where $q(z_0)=0$, $q'(z_0)\neq 0$:**
$$\text{Res}\!\left[\frac{p}{q}, z_0\right] = \frac{p(z_0)}{q'(z_0)}$$

This is just L'Hôpital applied to the simple-pole limit. Quick check: $\text{Res}[1/(z^2-1),\,1]$ — here $p = 1$, $q = z^2-1$, $q'(z) = 2z$, so the residue is $1/(2\cdot 1) = 1/2$.

<!-- STUDENT: Three residue-computation formulas are listed back-to-back without a worked example between them. The p/q′ formula in particular is not obvious — it comes from L'Hôpital applied to the simple-pole limit, but that derivation is omitted. Exercise 3 demonstrates it, but a quick illustration in the body (e.g. "for 1/(z²−1) at z=1: p(1)=1, q′(1)=2, residue=1/2") would help a reader who wants to understand rather than just memorise. -->

**At a pole of order $m$:**
$$\text{Res}[f, z_0] = \frac{1}{(m-1)!}\lim_{z \to z_0}\frac{d^{m-1}}{dz^{m-1}}\left[(z-z_0)^m f(z)\right]$$

Quick check: $\text{Res}[e^z/(z-1)^2,\, 1]$ — multiply by $(z-1)^2$ to get $e^z$, differentiate once (since $m=2$, so $m-1=1$), divide by $1! = 1$: $d(e^z)/dz\big|_{z=1} = e$.

---

## The residue theorem

**Residue theorem.** Let $f$ be analytic on and inside a simple closed contour $C$ (counterclockwise) except for isolated singularities $z_1, \ldots, z_k$ inside $C$. Then:

$$\oint_C f(z)\,dz = 2\pi i\sum_{j=1}^{k}\text{Res}[f, z_j]$$

This is the master formula of complex analysis. Cauchy's integral formula is the special case where $f$ has only simple poles.

---

## Evaluating real integrals

### Type 1: trigonometric integrals $\int_0^{2\pi} R(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\,d\theta$

Substitute $z = e^{i\theta}$: $\cos\theta = (z+z^{-1})/2$, $\sin\theta = (z-z^{-1})/(2i)$, $d\theta = dz/(iz)$. The integral becomes a contour integral on $|z| = 1$.

**Example.** $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{d\theta}{3 + 2\cos\theta}$. Substituting gives $\oint_{|z|=1}\frac{dz}{iz(3 + z + z^{-1})} = \oint_{|z|=1}\frac{dz}{i(z^2+3z+1)}$. The roots of $z^2+3z+1$ are $z = (-3\pm\sqrt{5})/2$; only $z_1 = (-3+\sqrt{5})/2 \approx -0.38$ lies inside $|z|=1$. Residue: $1/(i(2z_1+3)) = 1/(i\sqrt{5})$. Integral: $2\pi i \cdot 1/(i\sqrt{5}) = 2\pi/\sqrt{5}$. Exercise 5 follows the same pattern.

### Type 2: improper integrals $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} R(x)\,dx$

Close the contour with a large semicircle in the upper (or lower) half-plane. The semicircular arc's contribution vanishes as the radius grows — but the condition depends on the form of the integrand. For a plain rational $R(x)$ with no oscillatory factor, the ML estimation lemma guarantees the arc vanishes when the degree of the denominator exceeds the degree of the numerator by at least **2**. When the integrand takes the form $e^{iax}R(x)$ with $a > 0$ (for example, $e^{ix}/(1+x^2)$, whose real part gives the hook integral), **Jordan's lemma** applies and degree excess of at least **1** suffices. The residue theorem then gives the real integral as $2\pi i$ times the sum of residues in the upper half-plane.

<!-- STUDENT: "If R(x) → 0 fast enough" is vague. The engineer-prof already noted this: the precise condition is that the degree of the denominator exceeds the numerator's by at least 1. Without this, a reader applying the method to ∫ 1/(x+1) dx or similar won't know whether their problem qualifies. Even one sentence stating the condition explicitly would prevent misapplication. -->

**Example.** $\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{1+x^2}$. Poles of $1/(1+z^2)$: $z = \pm i$. Only $z = i$ is in the upper half-plane. Residue: $1/(2i)$. Integral: $2\pi i \cdot 1/(2i) = \pi$.

The hook integral $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\cos x/(1+x^2)\,dx$ uses the same idea with one extra step: write $\cos x = \text{Re}(e^{ix})$, so the integral equals $\text{Re}\!\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{ix}/(1+x^2)\,dx$. The integrand is now of the form $e^{iax}R(x)$ with $a=1$, so Jordan's lemma applies. The pole at $z=i$ gives residue $e^{i\cdot i}/(2i) = e^{-1}/(2i)$, and the integral equals $\text{Re}(2\pi i \cdot e^{-1}/(2i)) = \pi/e$.

<!-- VIZ: Residue theorem explorer — contour sweep. The complex plane shows domain colouring of a selectable rational function (default: 1/(1+z²), which has poles at ±i). Poles appear as white blooms in the colouring. A single slider controls the radius R of a circular contour centred at the origin (range 0.1 to 4.5). As R increases past each pole, that pole is highlighted in gold (#fbbf24) and the running residue sum updates in a panel below the plot. The panel shows: "Enclosed poles: [list]", "Sum of residues: [value]", "∮_C f dz = 2πi × ΣRes = [value]". For the 1/(1+z²) function, when R crosses |i| = 1, the integral jumps from 0 to π. The reader sees directly that each pole contributes exactly 2πi × (its residue). A second function option "1/((z²+1)(z²+4))" has four poles at ±i and ±2i; dragging R from 1 to 3 adds them one by one. Series thread: this is the culmination of the winding-number thread from Chapter 1 (winding number) and Chapter 2 (∮ dz/z = 2πi × n) — here the reader sees that residue = generalised winding contribution. -->

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const W = 400, H = 360, CX = W/2, CY = H/2, SCALE = 70;
  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  const funcData = {
    "1/(1+z²)": {
      poles: [{re:0,im:1,res:{re:0,im:-0.5},label:"i"},{re:0,im:-1,res:{re:0,im:0.5},label:"−i"}],
      realIntegral: "π",
      realValue: Math.PI,
      eval: (re,im) => {
        const dr=re, di=im+1, d=dr*dr+di*di;
        if(d<1e-8) return [NaN,NaN];
        const dr2=re, di2=im-1, d2=dr2*dr2+di2*di2;
        // 1/(z²+1) = 1/((z+i)(z-i))
        // just colour: use |f|
        // f = 1/(1+z^2): real = (1-y^2+x^2-2x^2)/... let's compute directly
        const r2 = 1 + re*re - im*im; const i2 = 2*re*im;
        const den = r2*r2 + i2*i2;
        if(den<1e-10) return [NaN,NaN];
        return [r2/den, -i2/den];
      }
    },
    "1/((z²+1)(z²+4))": {
      poles: [
        {re:0,im:1,res:{re:0,im:-1/6},label:"i"},
        {re:0,im:-1,res:{re:0,im:1/6},label:"−i"},
        {re:0,im:2,res:{re:0,im:1/12},label:"2i"},
        {re:0,im:-2,res:{re:0,im:-1/12},label:"−2i"}
      ],
      realIntegral: "π/6",
      realValue: Math.PI/6,
      eval: (re,im) => {
        // f = 1/((z^2+1)(z^2+4))
        const a1=re*re-im*im+1, b1=2*re*im, a2=re*re-im*im+4, b2=2*re*im;
        const ra=a1*a2-b1*b2, ia=a1*b2+a2*b1;
        const d=ra*ra+ia*ia; if(d<1e-10) return [NaN,NaN];
        return [ra/d,-ia/d];
      }
    },
    "z²/((z²−1)(z+2))": {
      poles: [
        {re:1,im:0,res:{re:1/6,im:0},label:"1"},
        {re:-1,im:0,res:{re:-1/2,im:0},label:"−1"},
        {re:-2,im:0,res:{re:4/3,im:0},label:"−2"}
      ],
      realIntegral: "(sum of residues)",
      realValue: null,
      eval: (re,im) => {
        const z2r=re*re-im*im, z2i=2*re*im;
        const d1r=z2r-1,d1i=z2i;
        const d2r=re+2,d2i=im;
        const d12r=d1r*d2r-d1i*d2i, d12i=d1r*d2i+d1i*d2r;
        const nd=d12r*d12r+d12i*d12i; if(nd<1e-10) return [NaN,NaN];
        return [(z2r*d12r+z2i*d12i)/nd,(z2i*d12r-z2r*d12i)/nd];
      }
    }
  };

  const funcSelector = Inputs.select(Object.keys(funcData), {
    value: "1/(1+z²)", label: "f(z)"
  });
  const radiusSlider = Inputs.range([0.1, 4.5], {value: 1.5, step: 0.05, label: "Contour radius R"});

  function hslToRgb(h,s,l) {
    h=((h%1)+1)%1;
    const c=(1-Math.abs(2*l-1))*s,x=c*(1-Math.abs((h*6)%2-1)),m=l-c/2;
    let r=0,g=0,b=0;
    if(h<1/6){r=c;g=x;}else if(h<2/6){r=x;g=c;}else if(h<3/6){g=c;b=x;}
    else if(h<4/6){g=x;b=c;}else if(h<5/6){r=x;b=c;}else{r=c;b=x;}
    return [Math.round((r+m)*255),Math.round((g+m)*255),Math.round((b+m)*255)];
  }

  function toScreen(re,im) { return [CX+re*SCALE, CY-im*SCALE]; }

  function render3(fname, R) {
    const fd = funcData[fname];

    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width=W; canvas.height=H;
    const ctx=canvas.getContext("2d");
    const img=ctx.createImageData(W,H); const data=img.data;

    for (let px=0;px<W;px++) {
      for (let py=0;py<H;py++) {
        const re=(px-CX)/SCALE, im=-(py-CY)/SCALE;
        const [wr,wi]=fd.eval(re,im);
        if(!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)) {
          const idx=(py*W+px)*4;
          data[idx]=255;data[idx+1]=255;data[idx+2]=255;data[idx+3]=255;
          continue;
        }
        const arg=Math.atan2(wi,wr), mag=Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue=(arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const logmag=Math.log(mag+0.001);
        const brightness=0.5+0.35*Math.tanh(logmag/2);
        const [r,g,b]=hslToRgb(hue,0.75,brightness);
        const idx=(py*W+px)*4;
        data[idx]=r;data[idx+1]=g;data[idx+2]=b;data[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    ctx.putImageData(img,0,0);

    // Contour
    const [cx0,cy0]=toScreen(0,0);
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.9)"; ctx.lineWidth=2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx0,cy0,R*SCALE,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)"; ctx.font="11px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText(`C: |z| = ${R.toFixed(2)}`,5,14);

    // Pole markers, labels, and winding number indicators
    const enclosed = [];
    fd.poles.forEach(p => {
      const [psx,psy]=toScreen(p.re,p.im);
      const inC = Math.sqrt(p.re*p.re+p.im*p.im) < R;
      if(inC) enclosed.push(p);
      ctx.strokeStyle=inC?"#fbbf24":"rgba(255,255,255,0.7)";
      ctx.lineWidth=2;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(psx-7,psy-7); ctx.lineTo(psx+7,psy+7); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(psx+7,psy-7); ctx.lineTo(psx-7,psy+7); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.fillStyle=inC?"#fbbf24":"rgba(255,255,255,0.7)";
      ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
      ctx.fillText(p.label,psx+9,psy+4);
      // Winding number badge — n=1 for each simple pole inside the contour
      if(inC) {
        ctx.fillStyle="#1e40af"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(psx-12,psy-12,10,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.fill();
        ctx.fillStyle="white"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign="center";
        ctx.fillText("n=1", psx-12, psy-8);
        ctx.textAlign="left";
        // Small label connecting to Ch1/Ch2
        ctx.fillStyle="#fbbf24"; ctx.font="9px sans-serif";
        ctx.fillText("winding=1", psx+9, psy+16);
      }
    });

    // Residue sum
    let sumRe=0, sumIm=0;
    enclosed.forEach(p => { sumRe+=p.res.re; sumIm+=p.res.im; });
    const integral2piRe = -2*Math.PI*sumIm;
    const integral2piIm = 2*Math.PI*sumRe;

    const infoDiv=document.createElement("div");
    infoDiv.style.cssText="margin-top:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.85em; background:#f0f9ff; border-radius:4px; padding:0.5rem;";
    const encStr=enclosed.length===0?"none":enclosed.map(p=>p.label).join(", ");
    const resStr=enclosed.length===0?"0":(`${sumRe.toFixed(4)}${sumIm>=0?"+":""}${sumIm.toFixed(4)}i`);
    const intStr=enclosed.length===0?"0":`${integral2piRe.toFixed(4)} + ${integral2piIm.toFixed(4)}i`;
    const realStr=(fd.realValue!==null&&enclosed.some(p=>p.im>0))
      ?`<div style="color:#059669">Real integral = \u22122\u03c0 \xd7 Im(\u03a3Res) = ${integral2piRe.toFixed(4)} [predicted: ${fd.realIntegral}]</div>`
      :"";
    const windingNote = enclosed.length>0
      ? `<div style="color:#1e40af; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:0.3rem;">Each enclosed pole has winding number n=1 (Ch1/Ch2: \u222e dz/z = 2\u03c0i \xd7 n). The residue theorem is this generalised: each pole contributes 2\u03c0i \xd7 n \xd7 Res.</div>`
      : "";
    infoDiv.innerHTML=`
      <div><strong>Enclosed poles:</strong> ${encStr}</div>
      <div><strong>Sum of residues:</strong> ${resStr}</div>
      <div><strong>\u222e<sub>C</sub> f\u202fdz = 2\u03c0i \xd7 \u03a3Res = </strong><span style="color:#1e40af">${intStr}</span></div>
      ${realStr}
      ${windingNote}
    `;

    const wrap=document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(canvas);
    wrap.appendChild(infoDiv);
    return wrap;
  }

  const container=document.createElement("div");
  container.style.cssText="border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const title=document.createElement("div");
  title.style.cssText="font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  title.textContent="Residue theorem explorer: sweeping poles with the contour";
  container.appendChild(title);
  container.appendChild(funcSelector);
  container.appendChild(radiusSlider);

  const vizDiv3=document.createElement("div");
  container.appendChild(vizDiv3);

  const note=document.createElement("div");
  note.style.cssText="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  note.textContent="Domain colouring shows f(z): poles appear as white blooms. Gold \u00d7 marks = poles inside contour; blue badge shows winding number n=1 for each simple pole (connecting to the Ch1/Ch2 winding-number thread: \u222e dz/z = 2\u03c0i \xd7 n). As R increases past each pole, the residue sum updates. Each pole contributes 2\u03c0i times its residue.";
  container.appendChild(note);

  function update3() {
    vizDiv3.innerHTML="";
    vizDiv3.appendChild(render3(funcSelector.value, radiusSlider.value));
  }
  funcSelector.addEventListener("input", update3);
  radiusSlider.addEventListener("input", update3);
  update3();

  return container;
}
```
