```{ojs}
        // e^{iz} = e^{i(re+iim)} = e^{-im}*(cos(re)+i*sin(re))
        const eR=Math.exp(-im)*Math.cos(re), eI=Math.exp(-im)*Math.sin(re);
        const a=1+re*re-im*im,b=2*re*im;const d=a*a+b*b;if(d<1e-10)return[NaN,NaN];
        return[(eR*a+eI*b)/d,(eI*a-eR*b)/d];
      },
      realResult:"π/e (real part)", realVal:Math.PI*Math.exp(-1),
      mlDegExcess: 1, jordanApplies: true,
      mlText: "Degree excess = 1. ML bound alone gives |arc| ≤ πR/(R²−1) → 0 only at O(1/R) — barely. Better: use Jordan's lemma.",
      jordanText: "Jordan's lemma applies: integrand = e^{iz}·R(z) with R(z)→0 uniformly. Arc integral → 0 for any degree excess ≥ 1 with oscillatory factor.",
      note: "Re(∫e^{ix}/(1+x²)dx) = π/e — the hook integral in the chapter."
    }
  };

  function hslToRgbSM(h,s,l) {
    h=((h%1)+1)%1;
    const c=(1-Math.abs(2*l-1))*s,x=c*(1-Math.abs((h*6)%2-1)),m=l-c/2;
    let r=0,g=0,b=0;
    if(h<1/6){r=c;g=x;}else if(h<2/6){r=x;g=c;}else if(h<3/6){g=c;b=x;}
    else if(h<4/6){g=x;b=c;}else if(h<5/6){r=x;b=c;}else{r=c;b=x;}
    return [Math.round((r+m)*255),Math.round((g+m)*255),Math.round((b+m)*255)];
  }

  function toScrSM(re,im) { return [CX_SM+re*SCALE_SM, CY_SM-im*SCALE_SM]; }

  function renderSM(fname, R, lemmaMode) {
    const fd = smFuncData[fname];

    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    canvas.width=W_SM; canvas.height=H_SM;
    const ctx=canvas.getContext("2d");
    const img=ctx.createImageData(W_SM,H_SM); const data=img.data;

    // Domain colouring — only upper half-plane
    for(let px=0;px<W_SM;px++) {
      for(let py=0;py<H_SM;py++) {
        const re=(px-CX_SM)/SCALE_SM, im=-(py-CY_SM)/SCALE_SM;
        if(im < -0.1) {
          const idx=(py*W_SM+px)*4; data[idx]=245;data[idx+1]=245;data[idx+2]=245;data[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const [wr,wi]=fd.eval(re,im);
        if(!isFinite(wr)||!isFinite(wi)||isNaN(wr)) {
          const idx=(py*W_SM+px)*4; data[idx]=255;data[idx+1]=255;data[idx+2]=255;data[idx+3]=255; continue;
        }
        const arg=Math.atan2(wi,wr),mag=Math.sqrt(wr*wr+wi*wi);
        const hue=(arg/(2*Math.PI)+1)%1;
        const brightness=0.5+0.35*Math.tanh(Math.log(mag+0.001)/2);
        // Dim below real axis
        const dimFactor = im < 0 ? 0.4 : 1.0;
        const [r,g,b]=hslToRgbSM(hue,0.8*dimFactor,0.5+(brightness-0.5)*dimFactor);
        const idx=(py*W_SM+px)*4; data[idx]=r;data[idx+1]=g;data[idx+2]=b;data[idx+3]=255;
      }
    }
    ctx.putImageData(img,0,0);

    const [ox,oy]=toScrSM(0,0);

    // Real axis (orange)
    ctx.strokeStyle="#f97316"; ctx.lineWidth=3;
    const [rx1]=toScrSM(-R-0.3,0); const [rx2]=toScrSM(R+0.3,0);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(rx1,oy); ctx.lineTo(rx2,oy); ctx.stroke();
    // Arrow at right end
    ctx.fillStyle="#f97316";
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(rx2,oy); ctx.lineTo(rx2-10,oy-5); ctx.lineTo(rx2-10,oy+5); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle="#f97316"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif"; ctx.fillText("real axis (−R to R)", rx1+4, oy+16);

    // Semicircle (blue)
    ctx.strokeStyle="#3b82f6"; ctx.lineWidth=2.5;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(ox,oy,R*SCALE_SM,Math.PI,0,false); ctx.stroke();
    // Arrow on semicircle
    const arcAngle = Math.PI/4;
    const arcX=ox+R*SCALE_SM*Math.cos(arcAngle), arcY=oy-R*SCALE_SM*Math.sin(arcAngle);
    ctx.strokeStyle="#3b82f6"; ctx.lineWidth=2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(arcX,arcY); ctx.lineTo(arcX-8,-8+arcY); ctx.lineTo(arcX+5,arcY-10); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="#3b82f6"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText(`Γ_R (R=${R.toFixed(2)})`, arcX+8, arcY-5);

    // R label on real axis
    const [rPx]=toScrSM(R,0); const [nrPx]=toScrSM(-R,0);
    ctx.fillStyle="#f97316"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("R", rPx+3, oy-6); ctx.fillText("−R", nrPx-20, oy-6);

    // Poles
    fd.poles.forEach(p => {
      const [psx,psy]=toScrSM(p.re,p.im);
      const inUpper = p.im > 0;
      const enclosed = inUpper && Math.sqrt(p.re*p.re+p.im*p.im) < R;

      ctx.strokeStyle=enclosed?"#fbbf24":"#dc2626"; ctx.lineWidth=2.5;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(psx-8,psy-8); ctx.lineTo(psx+8,psy+8); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(psx+8,psy-8); ctx.lineTo(psx-8,psy+8); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.fillStyle=enclosed?"#fbbf24":"#dc2626"; ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
      ctx.fillText(p.label, psx+10, psy+4);

      // Winding number badge for enclosed
      if(enclosed) {
        ctx.fillStyle="#1e40af"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(psx-14,psy-14,11,0,2*Math.PI); ctx.fill();
        ctx.fillStyle="white"; ctx.font="bold 9px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign="center";
        ctx.fillText("n=1", psx-14, psy-10);
        ctx.textAlign="left";
      }
    });

    // Axis labels
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.5)"; ctx.lineWidth=0.8;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(ox,0); ctx.lineTo(ox,H_SM); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(200,200,200,0.9)"; ctx.font="9px sans-serif";
    ctx.fillText("i", ox+3, oy-SCALE_SM+3); ctx.fillText("2i", ox+3, oy-2*SCALE_SM+3);

    // Result computation
    const encPoles = fd.poles.filter(p => p.im>0 && Math.sqrt(p.re*p.re+p.im*p.im)<R);
    let sumRe=0,sumIm=0;
    encPoles.forEach(p=>{sumRe+=p.res.re;sumIm+=p.res.im;});
    const intRe=-2*Math.PI*sumIm, intIm=2*Math.PI*sumRe;

    // Result box (green)
    if(encPoles.length>0) {
      ctx.fillStyle="rgba(5,150,105,0.92)";
      ctx.beginPath(); if(ctx.roundRect) ctx.roundRect(5,5,205,46,5); else ctx.rect(5,5,205,46); ctx.fill();
      ctx.fillStyle="white"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif";
      ctx.fillText("∮_C f dz = 2πi × ΣRes", 10, 20);
      ctx.font="10px sans-serif";
      const resultStr=`= ${intRe.toFixed(4)} + ${intIm.toFixed(4)}i`;
      ctx.fillText(resultStr, 10, 35);
      if(fd.realVal&&encPoles.some(p=>p.im>0)) {
        ctx.fillStyle="#bbf7d0"; ctx.font="9px sans-serif";
        ctx.fillText(`Real integral ≈ ${Math.abs(intRe).toFixed(4)} [exact: ${fd.realResult}]`, 10, 47);
      }
    }

    // Lemma annotation
    const lemmaText = lemmaMode==="Jordan's lemma" ? fd.jordanText : fd.mlText;
    const lemmaDiv = document.createElement("div");
    lemmaDiv.style.cssText="margin-top:0.4rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.83em; padding:0.4rem 0.6rem; border-radius:4px; background:#f0f9ff; border:1px solid #bfdbfe;";
    lemmaDiv.innerHTML=`<strong>${lemmaMode}:</strong> ${lemmaText}`;

    const infoDiv = document.createElement("div");
    infoDiv.style.cssText="margin-top:0.4rem; font-family:sans-serif; font-size:0.84em;";
    const encStr=encPoles.length===0?"none (R too small)":encPoles.map(p=>p.label).join(", ");
    infoDiv.innerHTML=`<strong>Enclosed poles (upper half-plane):</strong> ${encStr} — <em>${fd.note}</em>`;

    const wrap=document.createElement("div");
    wrap.appendChild(canvas); wrap.appendChild(infoDiv); wrap.appendChild(lemmaDiv);
    return wrap;
  }

  const containerSM=document.createElement("div");
  containerSM.style.cssText="border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem; margin:1rem 0;";
  const titleSM=document.createElement("div");
  titleSM.style.cssText="font-weight:600; margin-bottom:0.5rem; font-family:sans-serif;";
  titleSM.textContent="Semicircle contour closure: real integrals via the upper half-plane";
  containerSM.appendChild(titleSM);
  containerSM.appendChild(funcSelSM);
  containerSM.appendChild(rSliderSM);
  containerSM.appendChild(lemmaSel);
  const vizDivSM=document.createElement("div");
  containerSM.appendChild(vizDivSM);
  const noteSM=document.createElement("div");
  noteSM.style.cssText="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
  noteSM.textContent="Orange line = real axis −R to R; blue arc = semicircle Γ_R. Domain colouring shows f(z) in the upper half-plane. Red × = poles not yet enclosed; gold × = enclosed poles (winding number n=1 shown). Green box shows the integral result as R grows past each pole. Toggle the arc-vanishing argument between ML bound and Jordan's lemma.";
  containerSM.appendChild(noteSM);

  function updateSM(){
    vizDivSM.innerHTML="";
    vizDivSM.appendChild(renderSM(funcSelSM.value, parseFloat(rSliderSM.value), lemmaSel.value));
  }
  funcSelSM.addEventListener("input",updateSM);
  rSliderSM.addEventListener("input",updateSM);
  lemmaSel.addEventListener("input",updateSM);
  updateSM();

  return containerSM;
}
```

The residue theorem and Laurent series complete the core tools of complex integration. The next chapter takes a different direction: conformal mapping uses analytic functions to deform geometry — turning complicated domains into simple ones where Laplace's equation can be solved directly.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function makeStepperHTML(steps) {
  let current = 0;
  const totalSteps = steps.length;
  const container = document.createElement("div");
  container.style.cssText = "border:1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius:8px; padding:1rem 1.25rem; margin:0.75rem 0; font-family:inherit;";
  const stepsDiv = document.createElement("div");
  stepsDiv.style.marginBottom = "0.75rem";
  function renderSteps() {
    stepsDiv.innerHTML = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < current; i++) {
      const s = steps[i];
      const row = document.createElement("div");
      row.style.cssText = "display:grid; grid-template-columns:220px 1fr; gap:0.35rem 1rem; align-items:baseline; padding:0.35rem 0; border-top:1px solid #f3f4f6;";
      const opCell = document.createElement("span");
      opCell.style.cssText = "font-size:0.85em; color:#6b7280; font-style:italic;";
      opCell.textContent = s.op;
      const eqCell = document.createElement("span");
      eqCell.innerHTML = katex.renderToString(s.eq, { throwOnError: false, displayMode: false });
      row.appendChild(opCell); row.appendChild(eqCell);
      if (s.note) {
        const noteRow = document.createElement("div");
        noteRow.style.cssText = "grid-column:2; font-size:0.82em; color:#6b7280; padding-bottom:0.2rem;";
        noteRow.textContent = s.note;
        row.appendChild(noteRow);
      }
      stepsDiv.appendChild(row);
    }
    if (current === totalSteps) {
      const done = document.createElement("div");
      done.style.cssText = "margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.9em; color:#059669; font-weight:500;";
      done.textContent = "Solution complete.";
      stepsDiv.appendChild(done);
    }
  }
  const controls = document.createElement("div");
  controls.style.cssText = "display:flex; gap:0.5rem; align-items:center;";
  const nextBtn = document.createElement("button");
  nextBtn.textContent = "Next step →";
  nextBtn.style.cssText = "padding:0.42rem 0.95rem; border:1px solid #2563eb; border-radius:5px; background:#2563eb; color:#ffffff; cursor:pointer; font-size:0.9em; font-weight:600; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(37,99,235,0.18);";
  const resetBtn = document.createElement("button");
  resetBtn.textContent = "Reset";
  resetBtn.style.cssText = "padding:0.42rem 0.8rem; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius:5px; background:#f8fafc; cursor:pointer; font-size:0.9em; color:#475569; font-weight:500;";
  const counter = document.createElement("span");
  counter.style.cssText = "font-size:0.82em; color:#9ca3af; margin-left:0.25rem;";
  function updateButtons() {
    nextBtn.disabled = current === totalSteps;
    nextBtn.style.opacity = current === totalSteps ? "0.4" : "1";
    counter.textContent = current === 0 ? "Click to reveal steps" : `Step ${current} of ${totalSteps}`;
  }
  nextBtn.onclick = () => { if (current < totalSteps) { current++; renderSteps(); updateButtons(); } };
  resetBtn.onclick = () => { current = 0; renderSteps(); updateButtons(); };
  controls.appendChild(nextBtn); controls.appendChild(resetBtn); controls.appendChild(counter);
  container.appendChild(stepsDiv); container.appendChild(controls);
  renderSteps(); updateButtons();
  return container;
}
```

### Exercise 1: Laurent series around a pole

Find the Laurent series of $f(z) = \dfrac{1}{z(z-1)}$ valid for $0 < |z| < 1$, and classify the singularity at $z = 0$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Partial fractions",
    eq: "\\frac{1}{z(z-1)} = \\frac{A}{z} + \\frac{B}{z-1} \\implies A = -1,\\; B = 1",
    note: "Multiply both sides by z: at z=0, A = 1/(0−1) = −1. Multiply by (z−1): at z=1, B = 1/1 = 1."
  },
  {
    op: "Expand 1/(z−1) using geometric series for |z| < 1",
    eq: "\\frac{1}{z-1} = \\frac{-1}{1-z} = -\\sum_{n=0}^{\\infty}z^n"
  },
  {
    op: "Combine",
    eq: "\\frac{1}{z(z-1)} = -\\frac{1}{z} - 1 - z - z^2 - z^3 - \\cdots \\quad (0 < |z| < 1)"
  },
  {
    op: "Classify the singularity at z = 0",
    eq: "\\text{Principal part: } -1/z \\text{ (one term)} \\implies \\text{simple pole of order 1}",
    note: "The residue at z = 0 is the coefficient c_{−1} = −1."
  }
])
```

### Exercise 2: Classifying $\sin z / z^2$ at $z = 0$

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Expand sin z in Taylor series",
    eq: "\\sin z = z - \\frac{z^3}{6} + \\frac{z^5}{120} - \\cdots"
  },
  {
    op: "Divide by z²",
    eq: "\\frac{\\sin z}{z^2} = \\frac{1}{z} - \\frac{z}{6} + \\frac{z^3}{120} - \\cdots"
  },
  {
    op: "Principal part has one term: 1/z",
    eq: "\\text{Simple pole at } z = 0, \\quad \\text{Res}\\!\\left[\\frac{\\sin z}{z^2},\\, 0\\right] = 1"
  },
  {
    op: "Compare with sin(z)/z and sin(z)/z³",
    eq: "\\frac{\\sin z}{z} \\to 1 \\text{ (removable)}, \\quad \\frac{\\sin z}{z^3} \\text{ has principal part } 1/z^2 \\text{ (order-2 pole)}",
    note: "The order of the pole equals (order of zero of denominator) − (order of zero of numerator): z² has a zero of order 2 at 0; sin z has a zero of order 1; difference = 1."
  }
])
```

### Exercise 3: Residue at a simple pole

Find $\text{Res}\!\left[\dfrac{z^2+1}{(z-2)(z+3)},\; z=2\right]$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Apply the simple-pole formula",
    eq: "\\text{Res}[f, 2] = \\lim_{z\\to 2}(z-2)f(z) = \\lim_{z\\to 2}\\frac{z^2+1}{z+3}"
  },
  {
    op: "Evaluate at z = 2",
    eq: "= \\frac{4+1}{2+3} = \\frac{5}{5} = 1"
  },
  {
    op: "Alternatively, use p/q′ formula with q = (z−2)(z+3)",
    eq: "q'(z) = 2z+1, \\quad q'(2) = 5, \\quad p(2) = 5 \\implies \\text{Res} = 5/5 = 1 \\checkmark"
  }
])
```

### Exercise 4: Residue at a double pole

Find $\text{Res}\!\left[\dfrac{e^z}{(z-1)^2},\; z=1\right]$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Apply the order-m formula with m = 2",
    eq: "\\text{Res}[f,1] = \\frac{1}{(2-1)!}\\lim_{z\\to 1}\\frac{d}{dz}\\left[(z-1)^2\\cdot\\frac{e^z}{(z-1)^2}\\right] = \\lim_{z\\to 1}\\frac{d}{dz}e^z"
  },
  {
    op: "Evaluate",
    eq: "\\frac{d}{dz}e^z\\bigg|_{z=1} = e^1 = e"
  },
  {
    op: "Verify via Laurent expansion",
    eq: "\\frac{e^z}{(z-1)^2} = \\frac{e\\,e^{z-1}}{(z-1)^2} = \\frac{e}{(z-1)^2}\\left[1 + (z-1) + \\frac{(z-1)^2}{2} + \\cdots\\right] = \\frac{e}{(z-1)^2} + \\frac{e}{z-1} + \\cdots",
    note: "Coefficient of (z−1)^{−1} is e. ✓"
  }
])
```

### Exercise 5: Trigonometric integral

Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{d\theta}{2 + \cos\theta}$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Substitute z = e^{iθ}: cos θ = (z+1/z)/2, dθ = dz/(iz)",
    eq: "\\int_0^{2\\pi}\\frac{d\\theta}{2+\\cos\\theta} = \\oint_{|z|=1}\\frac{1}{2+\\frac{z+z^{-1}}{2}}\\cdot\\frac{dz}{iz} = \\oint_{|z|=1}\\frac{2\\,dz}{i(z^2+4z+1)}"
  },
  {
    op: "Find roots of z²+4z+1 = 0",
    eq: "z = \\frac{-4\\pm\\sqrt{12}}{2} = -2\\pm\\sqrt{3}",
    note: "z₁ = −2+√3 ≈ −0.27 (inside |z|=1); z₂ = −2−√3 ≈ −3.73 (outside)."
  },
  {
    op: "Compute Res[2/(i(z²+4z+1)), z₁]",
    eq: "\\text{Res} = \\frac{2}{i(2z_1+4)} = \\frac{2}{i\\cdot 2\\sqrt{3}} = \\frac{1}{i\\sqrt{3}} = \\frac{-i}{\\sqrt{3}}"
  },
  {
    op: "Apply the residue theorem",
    eq: "\\int_0^{2\\pi}\\frac{d\\theta}{2+\\cos\\theta} = 2\\pi i\\cdot\\frac{-i}{\\sqrt{3}} = \\frac{2\\pi}{\\sqrt{3}}"
  }
])
```

### Exercise 6: Improper real integral via residues

Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{dx}{(1+x^2)^2}$.

<!-- STEPPER -->
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
makeStepperHTML([
  {
    op: "Poles of 1/(1+z²)² at z = ±i, each of order 2",
    eq: "\\frac{1}{(1+z^2)^2} = \\frac{1}{(z-i)^2(z+i)^2}"
  },
  {
    op: "Close contour with upper semicircle; only z = i is in upper half-plane",
    eq: "\\text{Res}\\left[\\frac{1}{(z-i)^2(z+i)^2},\\,i\\right] = \\lim_{z\\to i}\\frac{d}{dz}\\frac{1}{(z+i)^2}"
  },
  {
    op: "Differentiate",
    eq: "\\frac{d}{dz}(z+i)^{-2} = -2(z+i)^{-3} \\implies \\text{Res} = \\frac{-2}{(2i)^3} = \\frac{-2}{-8i} = \\frac{1}{4i} = \\frac{-i}{4}"
  },
  {
    op: "Apply residue theorem (semicircle integral → 0 as R → ∞)",
    eq: "\\int_{-\\infty}^{\\infty}\\frac{dx}{(1+x^2)^2} = 2\\pi i\\cdot\\frac{-i}{4} = \\frac{2\\pi}{4} = \\frac{\\pi}{2}"
  }
])
```

## Chapter 03 — Series and residues
Layer: engineering

### Confusion points

1. **"Principal part" and "analytic part" named before their purpose is given** (§ Laurent series). The terms are introduced two paragraphs before the classification section that explains why they matter. A forward pointer in that paragraph would make the naming meaningful immediately.

2. **Picard's theorem cited without introduction** (§ Classification of isolated singularities, essential singularity). The reader has not seen this theorem before. Citing it without stating it or pointing to where it is proved makes the essential-singularity entry feel incomplete.

3. **The key "only c_{−1} survives" step relies on an unproven general result** (§ Residues, "Why it matters"). Chapter 2 proved the n=0 case of ∮(z−z₀)ⁿ dz = 0 or 2πi. This chapter extends it to all integers n without proof or back-reference. A sentence connecting it to the Chapter 2 result would close this gap.

4. **Three residue formulas in succession without an example** (§ Computing residues). The p/q′ formula is particularly non-obvious. The exercises cover all three formulas, but the body section is purely declarative. An inline micro-example for the p/q′ formula would help a reader who learns by seeing before doing.

5. **Jordan's lemma condition is vague** (§ Type 2 integrals). "If R(x) → 0 fast enough" does not tell the reader what "fast enough" means. The engineer-prof flagged this; from a student perspective it's a genuine trap — a reader will not know whether their integral qualifies.

### Reassurance gaps

- The hook integral (∫cos x / (1+x²) dx = π/e) is stated as motivation but never worked out in the chapter. The reader is shown the answer but not the three lines that produce it. An improper integral with a complex exponential requires one more step (taking the real part of ∫e^{ix}/(1+x²) dx) that isn't explained anywhere in the chapter. The Type 2 method only covers real rational R(x); the hook integral requires a small additional step that the chapter silently skips.

- After the residue theorem is stated, there is no brief worked example in the body (only in the exercises). The exercises cover this well, but a reader who wants to test their understanding before attempting an exercise has nowhere to check.

### Exercise calibration

- Exercises 1–6 form a good progression: Laurent series, singularity classification, simple pole, double pole, trigonometric integral, improper integral.
- Exercise 5 (trig integral) and Exercise 6 (double-pole improper integral) are appreciably harder than the earlier exercises. The jump in difficulty between Exercises 4 and 5 is large; readers who found Exercises 1–4 manageable may stall on Exercise 5.
- All exercises have clean answers. Good variety across field types (complex analysis, mechanics, algorithm analysis in destinations).

### Wayfinding

- The chapter's `opens_to` says "Conformal mapping" — but the hook says "this is the power of the residue theorem." A reader might expect the chapter to open into more integration applications, not conformal mapping. A sentence at the end of the body (before exercises) noting that conformal mapping is the next tool would reduce the apparent non-sequitur.

## Verdict: READABLE WITH FIXES

The chapter has strong exercises and the residue theorem is presented clearly. The main friction points are: the vague Jordan's lemma condition (a practical trap for engineers applying the method), the gap between the hook example and the technique actually demonstrated, and the three residue formulas presented without any inline example.
